Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verses 1–3:

(p-369) Surat al-Ahzab

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Prophet, fear God﴾. Although this is already known of his state, there are four aspects to His command to him concerning it:

The first: the meaning of this command is to increase in fearing God in the struggle against His enemies.

The second: the continuation of piety upon what had preceded in his state.

The third: that it is an address directed to him, while what is meant is others from his community.

The fourth: that the cause of the revelation of this verse is what is narrated, that "Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and Abu al-A'war al-Sulami came to Medina to renew the agreement of the Messenger of God ﷺ concerning a pact between him and them. They stayed with Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, al-Jadd ibn Qays and Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, and they conspired among themselves and came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and presented to him matters he disliked, all of them. The Messenger of God ﷺ and the Muslims intended to kill them, so God revealed: ﴿O Prophet, fear God﴾, meaning: in breaking the covenant that is between you and them, until the stipulated term for them."

(p-370) ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers﴾ from among the people of Mecca,

﴿and the hypocrites﴾ from among the people of Medina, in what they call you to.

﴿Indeed God is ever Knowing, Wise﴾. This may bear two meanings:

One: Knowing of their inner secrets, Wise in deferring them.

The second: Knowing of what is in the interest, Wise in the management.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن قَلْبَيْنِ﴾ فِيهِ سِتَّةُ أقاوِيلَ:

أحَدُها: «أنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قامَ يَوْمًا يُصَلِّي فَخَطَرَ خَطْرَةً فَقالَ المُنافِقُونَ الَّذِينَ يُصَلُّونَ مَعَهُ إنَّ لَهُ قَلْبَيْنِ قَلْبًا مَعَكم وقَلْبًا مَعَهم فَأنْزَلَ اللَّهُ هَذِهِ تَكْذِيبًا لَهُمْ;» قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ ويَكُونُ مَعْناهُ ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن جَسَدَيْنِ.

الثّانِي: أنَّ رَجُلًا مِن مُشْرِكِي قُرَيْشٍ مِن بَنِي فِهْرٍ قالَ: إنَّ في جَوْفِي قَلْبَيْنِ أعْقِلُ بِكُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنهُما أفْضَلَ مِن عَقْلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وكَذَبَ فَنَزَلَتْ فِيهِ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ.

وَيَكُونُ مَعْناهُ: ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن عَقْلَيْنِ.

الثّالِثُ: أنَّ جَمِيلَ بْنَ مَعْمَرٍ ويُكَنّى أبا مَعْمَرٍ مِن بَنِي جُمَحٍ كانَ أحْفَظَ النّاسِ لِما يَسْمَعُ وكانَ ذا فَهْمٍ ودَهاءٍ فَقالَتْ قُرَيْشٌ ما يَحْفَظُ جَمِيلٌ ما يَحْفَظُ بِقَلْبٍ واحِدٍ إنَّ لَهُ قَلْبَيْنِ فَلَمّا كانَ يَوْمُ بَدْرٍ وهُزِمُوا أفْلَتَ وفي يَدَيْهِ إحْدى نَعْلَيْهِ والأُخْرى في رِجْلَيْهِ فَلَقِيَهُ أبُو سُفْيانَ بِشاطِئِ البَحْرِ فاسْتَخْبَرَهُ فَأخْبَرَهُ أنَّ قُرَيْشًا قُتِلُوا وسَمّى مَن قُتِلَ مِن (p-٣٧١) أشْرافِهِمْ، قالَ لَهُ: إنَّهُ قَدْ ذَهَبَ عَقْلُكَ فَما بالُ نَعْلَيْكَ إحْداهُما في يَدِكَ والأُخْرى في رِجْلِكَ؟ قالَ: ما كُنْتُ أظُنُّها إلّا في رِجْلَيَّ فَظَهَرَ لَهم حالَهُ فَنَزَلَتْ فِيهِ الآيَةُ، قالَهُ السُّدِّيُّ ويَكُونُ مَعْناهُ: ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن فَهْمَيْنِ.

الرّابِعُ: أنَّ رَجُلًا كانَ يَقُولُ إنَّ لِي نَفْسَيْنِ نَفْسًا تَأْمُرُنِي ونَفْسًا تَنْهانِي فَنَزَلَ ذَلِكَ فِيهِ، قالَهُ الحَسَنُ ويَكُونُ مَعْناهُ: ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن نَفْسَيْنِ.

الخامِسُ: أنَّهُ مَثَلٌ ضَرَبَهُ اللَّهُ لِزَيْدِ بْنِ حارِثَةَ حِينَ تَبَنّاهُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ بَعْدَ أنْ أعْتَقَهُ فَلَمّا نَزَلَ تَحْرِيمُ التَّبَنِّي (tabanni, adoption) مُنِعَ مِنِ ادِّعائِهِ ولَدًا ونَزَلَ فِيهِ ﴿ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن قَلْبَيْنِ﴾ يَقُولُ: ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن أبَوَيْنِ، كَذَلِكَ لا يَكُونُ لِزَيْدٍ أبَوانِ حارِثَةُ ومُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ، قالَهُ مُقاتِلُ بْنُ حَيّانَ.

وَفِيهِ إثْباتٌ لِمَذْهَبِ الشّافِعِيِّ (al-Shafi'i) في نَفْيِ الوَلَدِ عَنْ أبَوَيْنِ ويَكُونُ مَعْناهُ: ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن أبَوَيْنِ.

السّادِسُ: مَعْناهُ: أنَّهُ لا يَكُونُ لِرَجُلٍ قَلْبٌ مُؤْمِنٌ مَعَنا وقَلْبٌ كافِرٌ عَلَيْنا لِأنَّهُ لا يَجْتَمِعُ الإيمانُ والكُفْرُ في قَلْبٍ واحِدٍ ويَكُونُ مَعْناهُ: ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن دِينَيْنِ، حَكاهُ النَّقّاشُ.

﴿وَما جَعَلَ أزْواجَكُمُ اللائِي تُظاهِرُونَ مِنهُنَّ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ﴾ وهو أنْ يَقُولَ لِزَوْجَتِهِ أنْتِ عَلَيَّ كَظَهْرِ أُمِّي، فَهَذا ظِهارٌ (zihar, a pre-Islamic form of divorce in which a husband likens his wife to his mother's back) كانُوا في الجاهِلِيَّةِ يُحَرِّمُونَ بِهِ الزَّوْجاتِ ويَجْعَلُونَهُنَّ في التَّحْرِيمِ كالأُمَّهاتِ، فَأبْطَلَ اللَّهُ بِذَلِكَ أنْ تَصِيرَ مُحَرَّمَةً كالأُمِّ لِأنَّها لَيْسَتْ بِأُمٍّ وأوْجَبَ عَلَيْهِ بِالظِّهارِ مِنها إذا صارَ فِيهِ عامِدًا كَفّارَةً ذَكَرَها في سُورَةِ المُجادِلَةِ ومَنَعَهُ مِن إصابَتِها حَتّى يُكَفِّرَ وسَنَذْكُرُ ذَلِكَ في مَوْضِعِهِ مِن هَذا الكِتابِ.

﴿وَما جَعَلَ أدْعِياءَكم أبْناءَكُمْ﴾ يَعْنِي بِذَلِكَ أدْعِياءَ النَّبِيِّ.

قالَ مُجاهِدٌ كانَ الرَّجُلُ في الجاهِلِيَّةِ يَكُونُ ذَلِيلًا فَيَأْتِي ذا القُوَّةِ والشَّرَفِ فَيَقُولُ: أنا ابْنُكَ فَيَقُولُ نَعَمْ فَإذا قَبِلَهُ واتَّخَذَهُ ابْنًا أصْبَحَ أعَزَّ أهْلِهِ وكانَ زَيْدُ بْنُ حارِثَةَ مِنهم قَدْ تَبَنّاهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ عَلى ما كانَ يَصْنَعُ أهْلُ الجاهِلِيَّةِ فَلَمّا جاءَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ أمَرَهُمُ اللَّهُ أنْ يُلْحِقُوهم بِآبائِهِمْ فَقالَ: ﴿وَما جَعَلَ أدْعِياءَكم أبْناءَكُمْ﴾ في الإسْلامِ.

(p-٣٧٢) ﴿ذَلِكم قَوْلُكم بِأفْواهِكُمْ﴾ أنَّ امْرَأتَهُ بِالظِّهارِ أُمُّهُ وأنَّ دَعِيَّهُ بِالتَّبَنِّي ابْنُهُ ﴿واللَّهُ يَقُولُ الحَقَّ﴾ في أنَّ الزَّوْجَةَ لا تَصِيرُ في الظِّهارِ أُمًّا والدَّعِيَّ لا يَصِيرُ بِالتَّبَنِّي ابْنًا.

﴿وَهُوَ يَهْدِي السَّبِيلَ﴾ يَعْنِي في إلْحاقِ النَّسَبِ بِالأبِ، وفي الزَّوْجَةِ أنَّها لا تَصِيرُ كالأُمِّ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ادْعُوهم لآبائِهِمْ﴾ يَعْنِي التَّبَنِّيَ: قالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ ما كُنّا نَدْعُو زَيْدَ بْنَ حارِثَةَ إلّا زَيْدَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ إلى أنْ نَزَلَ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ادْعُوهم لآبائِهِمْ﴾ قالَ السُّدِّيُّ فَدَعاهُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إلى حارِثَةَ وعَرِفَ كُلٌّ نَسَبَهُ فَأقَرُّوا بِهِ وأثْبَتُوا نَسَبَهُ.

﴿هُوَ أقْسَطُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ أيْ أعْدَلُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ قَوْلًا وحُكْمًا.

﴿فَإنْ لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا آباءَهم فَإخْوانُكم في الدِّينِ ومَوالِيكُمْ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أوْجُهٍ:

أحَدُها: فانْسُبُوهم إلى أسْماءِ إخْوانِكم ومُوالِيكم مِثْلَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وعُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ وعَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ وعَبْدِ الرَّحِيمِ وعَبْدِ العَزِيزِ، قالَهُ مُقاتِلُ بْنُ حَيّانَ.

الثّانِي: قُولُوا أخُونا فُلانٌ ووَلِيُّنا فُلانٌ، قالَهُ يَحْيى بْنُ سَلّامٍ.

وَرَوى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ المُنْكَدِرِ قالَ: جَلَسَ نَفَرٌ مِن أصْحابِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ مِنهم جابِرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الأنْصارِيُّ فَتَفاخَرُوا بِالآباءِ فَجَعَلَ كُلُّ واحِدٍ مِنهم يَقُولُ أنا فُلانُ بْنُ فُلانٍ حَتّى انْتَهَوْا إلى سَلْمانَ فَقالَ أنا سَلْمانُ ابْنُ الإسْلامِ فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ عُمَرَ بْنَ الخَطّابِ فَقالَ: صَدَقَ سَلْمانُ وأنا عُمَرُ بْنُ الإسْلامِ وذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَإخْوانُكم في الدِّينِ﴾.

الثّالِثُ: إنَّهُ إنْ لَمْ يُعْرَفْ لَهم أبٌ يُنْسَبُونَ إلَيْهِ كانُوا إخْوانًا إنْ كانُوا أحْرارًا، ومَوالِيَ إنْ كانُوا عُتَقاءَ كَما فَعَلَ المُسْلِمُونَ فِيمَن عَرَفُوا نَسَبَهُ وفِيمَن لَمْ يَعْرِفُوهُ فَإنَّ المِقْدادَ بْنَ عَمْرٍو كانَ يُقالُ لَهُ المِقْدادُ بْنُ الأسْوَدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ يَغُوثَ الزُّهْرِيُّ، فَرَجَعَ إلى أبِيهِ وسُفْيانُ بْنُ مَعْمَرٍ كانَتْ أُمُّهُ امْرَأةَ مَعْمَرٍ في الجاهِلِيَّةِ فادَّعاهُ ابْنًا ثُمَّ أسْلَمَ سُفْيانُ وشَهِدَ بَدْرًا فَنُسِبَ إلى أبِيهِ ونَسَبِهِ في بَنِي زُرَيْقٍ مِنَ الأنْصارِ.

وَمِمَّنْ لَمْ يُعْرَفْ لَهُ أبٌ سالِمٌ، مَوْلى أبِي حُذَيْفَةَ ونُسِبَ إلى ولاءِ أبِي حُذَيْفَةَ.

﴿وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكم جُناحٌ فِيما أخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ ولَكِنْ ما تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ:

أحَدُها: ما أخْطَأْتُمْ قَبْلَ النَّهْيِ وما تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكم بَعْدَ النَّهْيِ في هَذا وغَيْرِهِ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ.

(p-٣٧٣) الثّانِي: ما أخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ ما سَهَوْتُمْ عَنْهُ، وما تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكم ما قَصَدْتُمُوهُ عَنْ عَمْدٍ، قالَهُ حَبِيبُ بْنُ أبِي ثابِتٍ.

الثّالِثُ: ما أخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ أنْ تَدْعُوهُ إلى غَيْرِ أبِيهِ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ.

﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾ أيْ غَفُورًا عَمّا كانَ في الشِّرْكِ، رَحِيمًا بِقَبُولِ التَّوْبَةِ في الإسْلامِ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن قَلْبَيْنِ﴾ فِيهِ سِتَّةُ أقاوِيلَ:

أحَدُها: «أنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ قامَ يَوْمًا يُصَلِّي فَخَطَرَ خَطْرَةً فَقالَ المُنافِقُونَ الَّذِينَ يُصَلُّونَ مَعَهُ إنَّ لَهُ قَلْبَيْنِ قَلْبًا مَعَكم وقَلْبًا مَعَهم فَأنْزَلَ اللَّهُ هَذِهِ تَكْذِيبًا لَهُمْ;» قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ ويَكُونُ مَعْناهُ ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن جَسَدَيْنِ.

الثّانِي: أنَّ رَجُلًا مِن مُشْرِكِي قُرَيْشٍ مِن بَنِي فِهْرٍ قالَ: إنَّ في جَوْفِي قَلْبَيْنِ أعْقِلُ بِكُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنهُما أفْضَلَ مِن عَقْلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وكَذَبَ فَنَزَلَتْ فِيهِ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ.

وَيَكُونُ مَعْناهُ: ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن عَقْلَيْنِ.

الثّالِثُ: أنَّ جَمِيلَ بْنَ مَعْمَرٍ ويُكَنّى أبا مَعْمَرٍ مِن بَنِي جُمَحٍ كانَ أحْفَظَ النّاسِ لِما يَسْمَعُ وكانَ ذا فَهْمٍ ودَهاءٍ فَقالَتْ قُرَيْشٌ ما يَحْفَظُ جَمِيلٌ ما يَحْفَظُ بِقَلْبٍ واحِدٍ إنَّ لَهُ قَلْبَيْنِ فَلَمّا كانَ يَوْمُ بَدْرٍ وهُزِمُوا أفْلَتَ وفي يَدَيْهِ إحْدى نَعْلَيْهِ والأُخْرى في رِجْلَيْهِ فَلَقِيَهُ أبُو سُفْيانَ بِشاطِئِ البَحْرِ فاسْتَخْبَرَهُ فَأخْبَرَهُ أنَّ قُرَيْشًا قُتِلُوا وسَمّى مَن قُتِلَ مِن (p-٣٧١) أشْرافِهِمْ، قالَ لَهُ: إنَّهُ قَدْ ذَهَبَ عَقْلُكَ فَما بالُ نَعْلَيْكَ إحْداهُما في يَدِكَ والأُخْرى في رِجْلِكَ؟ قالَ: ما كُنْتُ أظُنُّها إلّا في رِجْلَيَّ فَظَهَرَ لَهم حالَهُ فَنَزَلَتْ فِيهِ الآيَةُ، قالَهُ السُّدِّيُّ ويَكُونُ مَعْناهُ: ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن فَهْمَيْنِ.

الرّابِعُ: أنَّ رَجُلًا كانَ يَقُولُ إنَّ لِي نَفْسَيْنِ نَفْسًا تَأْمُرُنِي ونَفْسًا تَنْهانِي فَنَزَلَ ذَلِكَ فِيهِ، قالَهُ الحَسَنُ ويَكُونُ مَعْناهُ: ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن نَفْسَيْنِ.

الخامِسُ: أنَّهُ مَثَلٌ ضَرَبَهُ اللَّهُ لِزَيْدِ بْنِ حارِثَةَ حِينَ تَبَنّاهُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ بَعْدَ أنْ أعْتَقَهُ فَلَمّا نَزَلَ تَحْرِيمُ التَّبَنِّي (tabanni, adoption) مُنِعَ مِنِ ادِّعائِهِ ولَدًا ونَزَلَ فِيهِ ﴿ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن قَلْبَيْنِ﴾ يَقُولُ: ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن أبَوَيْنِ، كَذَلِكَ لا يَكُونُ لِزَيْدٍ أبَوانِ حارِثَةُ ومُحَمَّدٌ ﷺ، قالَهُ مُقاتِلُ بْنُ حَيّانَ.

وَفِيهِ إثْباتٌ لِمَذْهَبِ الشّافِعِيِّ (al-Shafi'i) في نَفْيِ الوَلَدِ عَنْ أبَوَيْنِ ويَكُونُ مَعْناهُ: ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن أبَوَيْنِ.

السّادِسُ: مَعْناهُ: أنَّهُ لا يَكُونُ لِرَجُلٍ قَلْبٌ مُؤْمِنٌ مَعَنا وقَلْبٌ كافِرٌ عَلَيْنا لِأنَّهُ لا يَجْتَمِعُ الإيمانُ والكُفْرُ في قَلْبٍ واحِدٍ ويَكُونُ مَعْناهُ: ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِرَجُلٍ مِن دِينَيْنِ، حَكاهُ النَّقّاشُ.

﴿وَما جَعَلَ أزْواجَكُمُ اللائِي تُظاهِرُونَ مِنهُنَّ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ﴾ وهو أنْ يَقُولَ لِزَوْجَتِهِ أنْتِ عَلَيَّ كَظَهْرِ أُمِّي، فَهَذا ظِهارٌ (zihar, a pre-Islamic form of divorce in which a husband likens his wife to his mother's back) كانُوا في الجاهِلِيَّةِ يُحَرِّمُونَ بِهِ الزَّوْجاتِ ويَجْعَلُونَهُنَّ في التَّحْرِيمِ كالأُمَّهاتِ، فَأبْطَلَ اللَّهُ بِذَلِكَ أنْ تَصِيرَ مُحَرَّمَةً كالأُمِّ لِأنَّها لَيْسَتْ بِأُمٍّ وأوْجَبَ عَلَيْهِ بِالظِّهارِ مِنها إذا صارَ فِيهِ عامِدًا كَفّارَةً ذَكَرَها في سُورَةِ المُجادِلَةِ ومَنَعَهُ مِن إصابَتِها حَتّى يُكَفِّرَ وسَنَذْكُرُ ذَلِكَ في مَوْضِعِهِ مِن هَذا الكِتابِ.

﴿وَما جَعَلَ أدْعِياءَكم أبْناءَكُمْ﴾ يَعْنِي بِذَلِكَ أدْعِياءَ النَّبِيِّ.

قالَ مُجاهِدٌ كانَ الرَّجُلُ في الجاهِلِيَّةِ يَكُونُ ذَلِيلًا فَيَأْتِي ذا القُوَّةِ والشَّرَفِ فَيَقُولُ: أنا ابْنُكَ فَيَقُولُ نَعَمْ فَإذا قَبِلَهُ واتَّخَذَهُ ابْنًا أصْبَحَ أعَزَّ أهْلِهِ وكانَ زَيْدُ بْنُ حارِثَةَ مِنهم قَدْ تَبَنّاهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ عَلى ما كانَ يَصْنَعُ أهْلُ الجاهِلِيَّةِ فَلَمّا جاءَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ أمَرَهُمُ اللَّهُ أنْ يُلْحِقُوهم بِآبائِهِمْ فَقالَ: ﴿وَما جَعَلَ أدْعِياءَكم أبْناءَكُمْ﴾ في الإسْلامِ.

(p-٣٧٢) ﴿ذَلِكم قَوْلُكم بِأفْواهِكُمْ﴾ أنَّ امْرَأتَهُ بِالظِّهارِ أُمُّهُ وأنَّ دَعِيَّهُ بِالتَّبَنِّي ابْنُهُ ﴿واللَّهُ يَقُولُ الحَقَّ﴾ في أنَّ الزَّوْجَةَ لا تَصِيرُ في الظِّهارِ أُمًّا والدَّعِيَّ لا يَصِيرُ بِالتَّبَنِّي ابْنًا.

﴿وَهُوَ يَهْدِي السَّبِيلَ﴾ يَعْنِي في إلْحاقِ النَّسَبِ بِالأبِ، وفي الزَّوْجَةِ أنَّها لا تَصِيرُ كالأُمِّ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ادْعُوهم لآبائِهِمْ﴾ يَعْنِي التَّبَنِّيَ: قالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ ما كُنّا نَدْعُو زَيْدَ بْنَ حارِثَةَ إلّا زَيْدَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ إلى أنْ نَزَلَ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿ادْعُوهم لآبائِهِمْ﴾ قالَ السُّدِّيُّ فَدَعاهُ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ إلى حارِثَةَ وعَرِفَ كُلٌّ نَسَبَهُ فَأقَرُّوا بِهِ وأثْبَتُوا نَسَبَهُ.

﴿هُوَ أقْسَطُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ أيْ أعْدَلُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ قَوْلًا وحُكْمًا.

﴿فَإنْ لَمْ تَعْلَمُوا آباءَهم فَإخْوانُكم في الدِّينِ ومَوالِيكُمْ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أوْجُهٍ:

أحَدُها: فانْسُبُوهم إلى أسْماءِ إخْوانِكم ومُوالِيكم مِثْلَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وعُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ وعَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ وعَبْدِ الرَّحِيمِ وعَبْدِ العَزِيزِ، قالَهُ مُقاتِلُ بْنُ حَيّانَ.

الثّانِي: قُولُوا أخُونا فُلانٌ ووَلِيُّنا فُلانٌ، قالَهُ يَحْيى بْنُ سَلّامٍ.

وَرَوى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ المُنْكَدِرِ قالَ: جَلَسَ نَفَرٌ مِن أصْحابِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ مِنهم جابِرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الأنْصارِيُّ فَتَفاخَرُوا بِالآباءِ فَجَعَلَ كُلُّ واحِدٍ مِنهم يَقُولُ أنا فُلانُ بْنُ فُلانٍ حَتّى انْتَهَوْا إلى سَلْمانَ فَقالَ أنا سَلْمانُ ابْنُ الإسْلامِ فَبَلَغَ ذَلِكَ عُمَرَ بْنَ الخَطّابِ فَقالَ: صَدَقَ سَلْمانُ وأنا عُمَرُ بْنُ الإسْلامِ وذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَإخْوانُكم في الدِّينِ﴾.

الثّالِثُ: إنَّهُ إنْ لَمْ يُعْرَفْ لَهم أبٌ يُنْسَبُونَ إلَيْهِ كانُوا إخْوانًا إنْ كانُوا أحْرارًا، ومَوالِيَ إنْ كانُوا عُتَقاءَ كَما فَعَلَ المُسْلِمُونَ فِيمَن عَرَفُوا نَسَبَهُ وفِيمَن لَمْ يَعْرِفُوهُ فَإنَّ المِقْدادَ بْنَ عَمْرٍو كانَ يُقالُ لَهُ المِقْدادُ بْنُ الأسْوَدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ يَغُوثَ الزُّهْرِيُّ، فَرَجَعَ إلى أبِيهِ وسُفْيانُ بْنُ مَعْمَرٍ كانَتْ أُمُّهُ امْرَأةَ مَعْمَرٍ في الجاهِلِيَّةِ فادَّعاهُ ابْنًا ثُمَّ أسْلَمَ سُفْيانُ وشَهِدَ بَدْرًا فَنُسِبَ إلى أبِيهِ ونَسَبِهِ في بَنِي زُرَيْقٍ مِنَ الأنْصارِ.

وَمِمَّنْ لَمْ يُعْرَفْ لَهُ أبٌ سالِمٌ، مَوْلى أبِي حُذَيْفَةَ ونُسِبَ إلى ولاءِ أبِي حُذَيْفَةَ.

﴿وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكم جُناحٌ فِيما أخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ ولَكِنْ ما تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ:

أحَدُها: ما أخْطَأْتُمْ قَبْلَ النَّهْيِ وما تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكم بَعْدَ النَّهْيِ في هَذا وغَيْرِهِ، قالَهُ مُجاهِدٌ.

(p-٣٧٣) الثّانِي: ما أخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ ما سَهَوْتُمْ عَنْهُ، وما تَعَمَّدَتْ قُلُوبُكم ما قَصَدْتُمُوهُ عَنْ عَمْدٍ، قالَهُ حَبِيبُ بْنُ أبِي ثابِتٍ.

الثّالِثُ: ما أخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ أنْ تَدْعُوهُ إلى غَيْرِ أبِيهِ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ.

﴿وَكانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا﴾ أيْ غَفُورًا عَمّا كانَ في الشِّرْكِ، رَحِيمًا بِقَبُولِ التَّوْبَةِ في الإسْلامِ.

**The Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves** (﴿النَّبِيُّ أوْلى بِالمُؤْمِنِينَ مِن أنْفُسِهِمْ﴾). On this verse there are four views:

First: he is closer to them than they are to one another, because he was sent to them and their obedience to him is obligatory. This is the view of Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

Second: he is closer to them in what he sees as good for them, more than they see it for themselves. This is the view of Ikrimah.

Third: he was, in the first sense, a father to them.

The occasion of revelation was that "when the Prophet (ﷺ) wanted to go on the expedition to Tabuk, he ordered the people to set out. Some of them said: 'We will ask permission from our fathers and our mothers.' So Allah revealed this verse about them." This is related by al-Naqqash.

Fourth: he is closer to them in settling their debts and helping them in their hardships, according to what ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi ʿAmra transmitted from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no believer except that I am the closest of people to him in this world and the Hereafter. Recite if you wish: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves﴾. So whichever believer leaves wealth, his heirs, whoever they are, shall inherit it; and if he leaves debt or dependents, let him come to me, for I am his guardian."

﴿And his wives are their mothers﴾. This means that the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who died leaving him are like mothers in two respects:

First: the honouring of their rights.

Second: the prohibition of marrying them.

They are not like mothers with regard to maintenance (nafaqah) and inheritance.

Scholars differed on whether they are like mothers regarding mahram status (a relative one may never marry) and permission to look at them, and there are two positions:

First: they are mahram, so looking at them is not forbidden, because marriage to them is prohibited.

Second: looking at them is forbidden, because the prohibition of marrying them was only to protect the right of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning them. Part of protecting his right was forbidding looking at them. Also, ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, when she wanted a man to enter upon her, would order her sister Asma to nurse him, so that he would become her nephew through foster-nursing and thus a mahram whose presence is permitted.

As for those whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divorced during his lifetime, there are three views on whether this prohibition applies to them:

First: this prohibition applies to them, giving precedence to the sanctity of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Second: it does not apply to them; rather, they are like all other women, because the Prophet (ﷺ) had already established their chastity (ʿiṣmah) and said: "My wives in this world are my wives in the Hereafter."

Third: whoever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had consummated the marriage with, her prohibition applies and her marriage is forbidden even if he divorced her, in protection of his sanctity and guarding his privacy. Whoever he had not consummated the marriage with does not acquire this prohibition. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab once intended to stone a woman whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had separated from, and she had married after him. She said: "Why is this? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not place a veil upon me, nor was I named a mother to the believers." So he refrained from her.

Since the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) are the mothers of the believers in what we have mentioned, scholars differed on whether they are also mothers of the believing women, and there are two views:

First: they are mothers of the believing men and women, honouring their rights over men and women alike.

Second: this ruling is specific to the believing men and not the women, because the prohibition and permission (of looking and the like) pertain to men and not to women.

Al-Shaʿbi transmitted from Masruq, from ʿAʾishah, that a woman said to her, "O mother," and she replied: "I am not a mother to you; I am the mother of your men."

﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another in the Book of Allah than the believers and the emigrants﴾. It is said that by "the believers" he meant the Helpers (al-Ansar), and by "the emigrants" he meant the Quraysh.

On this there are two views:

First: this verse abrogates (naskh) inheritance through emigration. Saʿid transmitted from Qatadah, who said: In the chapter of al-Anfal had been revealed: ﴿Those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no guardianship over them until they emigrate﴾. So the Muslims inherited from one another on the basis of emigration, and a Bedouin Muslim would not inherit anything from his emigrant Muslim relative. Then this was abrogated in this surah by His saying: ﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another﴾.

Second: this verse abrogates inheritance through alliance (hilf) and brotherhood in religion (muʾākhāh). Hisham ibn ʿAmr transmitted from his father, from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam, who said: "It was revealed concerning us specifically, the group of the Quraysh and the Helpers. When we arrived in Medina, we arrived with no wealth. We found the Helpers to be excellent brothers, so we made brotherhood with them, and they made us their heirs and we made them our heirs. Abu Bakr made brotherhood with Kharijah ibn Zayd, and I made brotherhood with Kaʿb ibn Malik. When the Day of Uhud came, Kaʿb ibn Malik was killed, and I came and found that his weapons had weighed him down. By Allah, the one who died did not have anyone other than me to inherit from him, until Allah revealed this verse, and we returned to our inheritances."

His saying ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾ has two views:

First: in the Qur'an. This is the view of Qatadah.

Second: in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), which decrees the states of His creation. This is the view of Ibn Bahr.

**Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on Surah 33, verses 9–10:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: he means the Day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), when Allah bestowed upon them patience and then victory.

﴿When there came upon you hosts﴾. Mujahid said: the hosts of the Confederates were Abu Sufyan, ʿUyaynah ibn Husayn, Talhah ibn Khuwaylid, Abu al-Aʿwar al-Sulami, and the Banu Qurayzah.

﴿So We sent against them a wind﴾. Mujahid said: it was the eastern wind (al-Saba), which was sent upon the Confederates on the Day of the Trench (al-Khandaq), until it overturned their cooking pots and uprooted their tent pegs. Ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been helped by the eastern wind, and ʿAd were destroyed by the western wind (al-Dabur)." And among his supplications on the Day of the Confederates was: "O Allah, conceal our nakedness and secure our fears." So Allah struck the faces of His enemies with the eastern wind.

(p-379) ﴿And hosts you did not see﴾. Mujahid and Qatadah said: they were the angels.

Concerning what they did, there are four opinions:

The first: the dispersal of the word of the polytheists and the setting of some of them against others.

The second: the casting of terror into their hearts, related by Ibn Shajarah.

The third: the strengthening of the souls of the Muslims without their fighting alongside them. The wind helped them by driving the enemy away until it carried them beyond a distance of three days' journey. Then Talhah ibn Khuwaylid said: "Muhammad has begun to cast a spell upon you, so [seek] safety, safety!"

﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do﴾. He means: of digging the trench and guarding against the enemy.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾. He means: from above the valley, which is its upper part, on the side of the east. From it came ʿAwf ibn Malik with the Banu Nadr, ʿUyaynah ibn Husayn with the people of Najd, and Talhah ibn Khuwaylid al-Asadi with the Banu Asad.

﴿And from below you﴾. He means: from the bottom of the valley, on the side of the west, "below" meaning beneath the Prophet (ﷺ). From it came Abu Sufyan ibn Harb with the people of Makkah, Yazid ibn Jahsh with the Quraysh, and Abu al-Aʿwar al-Sulami came with Huyayy ibn Akhtab the Jew among the Jews of the Banu Qurayzah, together with ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, from the direction of the trench.

﴿And when the eyes shifted﴾. Concerning this there are two meanings:

One: they became fixed in their sockets (from terror).

The second: they turned aside.

﴿And the hearts reached the throats﴾. That is, they moved from their places until the hearts reached the throats, which are the gullets; its singular is ḥanjarah.

It has been said that this is a figure of speech used for extreme fear, that the hearts reached the throats, even though they did not actually leave their places while life remained.

It is narrated "from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri that he said on the Day of the Trench: 'O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), will you command us to say something, for the hearts have reached the throats?' He said: 'Yes, say: O Allah, conceal our nakedness and secure our fears.' He said: so Allah struck the faces of His enemies with the wind, and they were routed by it."

﴿And you thought about Allah assumptions﴾. Concerning this there are two meanings:

One: concerning what they were promised of victory. This was said by al-Suddi.

The second: it refers to the divergence of their assumptions. The hypocrites thought that Muhammad and his companions would be uprooted, while the believers were certain that what Allah and His Messenger had promised them was true, and that He would make it prevail over all religion, even though the polytheists dislike it. This was said by al-Hasan.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 11–13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There the believers were tested﴾, has three interpretations:

First: by confinement (al-hasr). This is related by al-Naqqash.

Second: by hunger, for a severe hunger afflicted them at the Trench (al-Khandaq). This is said by al-Dahhak.

Third: they were tested in patience upon their faith, and the believers were distinguished from the hypocrites. This is related by Ibn Shajarah.

Ibn ʿIsa related that ﴿hunalika﴾ (there) indicates a distant place, *hunaka* indicates a middle distance, and *huna* indicates a near place.

﴿And they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾ has four interpretations:

First: they were moved by fear with a severe movement. This is said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Second: it was their disturbance from what they were upon; among them were those whose self was disturbed, and among them those whose religion was disturbed.

Third: the command to steadfastness and patience moved them, and this is a possibility.

Fourth: it was their displacement from their places, until they had nothing but the place of the Trench. This is said by al-Dahhak.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease said﴾ has two interpretations:

First: the disease is hypocrisy. This is said by Qatadah.

Second: it is polytheism (al-shirk). This is said by al-Hasan.

﴿What Allah and His Messenger promised us was nothing but delusion﴾. Al-Suddi related that the Prophet ﷺ was digging the Trench for the battle of the Confederates (al-Ahzab). While he was striking in it with his pickaxe, the pickaxe struck a boulder, and a spark flew from it like a shooting flame into the sky. He struck a second time and the same came out, and he struck a third time and the same came out. Salman saw that, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Did you see what came out with every blow you struck?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "The white cities (bayd al-madaʾin), the palaces of the Romans, and the cities of Yemen will be opened for you." He said: So this spread among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and they discussed it. Then a man from the Ansar called Qushayr ibn Muʿattib — and others said Qushayr ibn ʿAdiyy al-Ansari of the Aws — said: "Muhammad promises us that the cities of Yemen, the palaces of the Romans and the white cities will be opened for us, while one of us cannot relieve himself without being killed? By Allah, this is delusion." So Allah revealed this verse.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when a group of them said﴾ — meaning of the hypocrites. It is said they were of the Banu Salim. It is also said it was the statement of Aws ibn Fayzi and whoever agreed with his opinion; Yazid ibn Ruman mentioned this. Al-Suddi related that it was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions.

﴿O people of Yathrib, there is no place (muqam) for you, so return﴾. Hafs, from ʿAsim, read *muqama* with a dammah on the mim, and the rest read it with a fatha.

Regarding the difference between them there are two views:

First: the view of al-Farra' is that *maqam* with a fatha means steadfastness upon a matter, and with a dammah means remaining in a place.

Second: the view of Ibn al-Mubarak is that with a fatha it means dwelling (manzil), and with a dammah it means residence (iqamah).

As for its interpretation, there are three views:

First: meaning, there is no place for you upon the religion of Muhammad, so return to the religion of the Arab polytheists. This is said by al-Hasan.

Second: there is no place for you in fighting, so return to seeking safety. This is said by al-Kalbi.

Third: there is no place for you where you are, so return to your homes. Al-Naqqash said this.

What is meant by Yathrib is Medina, and regarding this there are two views:

First: that Yathrib is Medina. This is related by Ibn ʿIsa.

Second: that Medina is a district within Yathrib. This is said by Abu ʿUbayda. Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad narrated from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever says 'Medina is Yathrib' let him seek forgiveness from Allah; it is Taba (Ṭābah)" — three times.

﴿And a party of them sought permission from the Prophet﴾. Al-Suddi said: those who sought permission from him were two men of the Ansar from the Banu Harithah, one of them Abu ʿUrabah ibn Aws, and the other Aws ibn Fayzi.

Al-Dahhak said: eighty men returned without permission.

﴿They said: Indeed our houses are exposed (ʿawrah)﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

First: they are remote from Medina; we fear for the nakedness (ʿawrah) of the women and children from captivity. This is said by Qatadah.

Second: they are empty, having nothing in them but the ʿawrah of the women. This is said by al-Kalbi and al-Farra', derived from their saying: "the horseman has become ʿawwara" when there is a gap in him for a blow. The poet said:

*Lahu al-shiddatu al-ula idha al-qarnu aʿwara*

Third: their walls are uncovered; we fear for them thieves and pursuers. This is said by al-Suddi. The Arabs say: "your dwelling has become aʿwar" when its covering has gone and its wall has fallen, and everything whose exposure is disliked is for them an ʿawrah. Ibn ʿAbbas read *inna buyutana ʿawiratun* with a kasra on the waw, meaning liable to be exposed.

Then He said: ﴿And they were not exposed﴾, refuting them in what they claimed.

﴿They intend nothing but flight﴾ may bear two meanings:

First: flight from being killed.

Second: flight from the religion.

Al-Naqqash related that this verse was revealed concerning two tribes of the Ansar, the Banu Harithah and the Banu Salamah, who intended to abandon their posts on the day of the Trench; and concerning them Allah revealed: ﴿When two parties among you were about to lose heart﴾ [Al ʿImran: 122], the verse.

When this verse was revealed they said: "By Allah, what we had intended does not please us, if Allah is our Protector."

The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "The white cities (bayd al-madaʾin), the palaces of the Romans, and the cities of Yemen will be opened for you." He said: So this spread among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and they discussed it. Then a man from the Ansar called Qushayr ibn Muʿattib — and others said Qushayr ibn ʿAdiyy al-Ansari of the Aws — said: "Muhammad promises us that the cities of Yemen, the palaces of the Romans and the white cities will be opened for us, while one of us cannot relieve himself without being killed? By Allah, this is delusion." So Allah revealed this verse.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when a group of them said﴾ — meaning of the hypocrites. It is said they were of the Banu Salim. It is also said it was the statement of Aws ibn Fayzi and whoever agreed with his opinion; Yazid ibn Ruman mentioned this. Al-Suddi related that it was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions.

﴿O people of Yathrib, there is no place (muqam) for you, so return﴾. Hafs, from ʿAsim, read *muqama* with a dammah on the mim, and the rest read it with a fatha.

Regarding the difference between them there are two views:

First: the view of al-Farra' is that *maqam* with a fatha means steadfastness upon a matter, and with a dammah means remaining in a place.

Second: the view of Ibn al-Mubarak is that with a fatha it means dwelling (manzil), and with a dammah it means residence (iqamah).

As for its interpretation, there are three views:

First: meaning, there is no place for you upon the religion of Muhammad, so return to the religion of the Arab polytheists. This is said by al-Hasan.

Second: there is no place for you in fighting, so return to seeking safety. This is said by al-Kalbi.

Third: there is no place for you where you are, so return to your homes. Al-Naqqash said this.

What is meant by Yathrib is Medina, and regarding this there are two views:

First: that Yathrib is Medina. This is related by Ibn ʿIsa.

Second: that Medina is a district within Yathrib. This is said by Abu ʿUbayda. Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad narrated from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever says 'Medina is Yathrib' let him seek forgiveness from Allah; it is Taba (Ṭābah)" — three times.

﴿And a party of them sought permission from the Prophet﴾. Al-Suddi said: those who sought permission from him were two men of the Ansar from the Banu Harithah, one of them Abu ʿUrabah ibn Aws, and the other Aws ibn Fayzi.

Al-Dahhak said: eighty men returned without permission.

﴿They said: Indeed our houses are exposed (ʿawrah)﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

First: they are remote from Medina; we fear for the nakedness (ʿawrah) of the women and children from captivity. This is said by Qatadah.

Second: they are empty, having nothing in them but the ʿawrah of the women. This is said by al-Kalbi and al-Farra', derived from their saying: "the horseman has become ʿawwara" when there is a gap in him for a blow. The poet said:

Third: their walls are uncovered; we fear for them thieves and pursuers. This is said by al-Suddi. The Arabs say: "your dwelling has become aʿwar" when its covering has gone and its wall has fallen, and everything whose exposure is disliked is for them an ʿawrah. Then He said: ﴿And they were not exposed﴾, refuting them in what they claimed.

﴿They intend nothing but flight﴾ may bear two meanings:

First: flight from being killed.

Second: flight from the religion.

Al-Naqqash related that this verse was revealed concerning two tribes of the Ansar, the Banu Harithah and the Banu Salamah, who intended to abandon their posts on the day of the Trench; and concerning them Allah revealed: ﴿When two parties among you were about to lose heart﴾ [Al ʿImran: 122], the verse.

When this verse was revealed they said: "By Allah, what we had intended does not please us, if Allah is our Protector."

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verses 14–17:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And if they had been entered upon from all its sides﴾ means: if the enemy had entered upon the hypocrites from the sides (aqtar) of Madinah and its surroundings (nawahi).

﴿Then they were asked for fitnah (strife), they would have given it﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

The first: they would not have delayed in responding to the strife except briefly. This was said by Ibn 'Isa.

The second: they would not have remained in Madinah except briefly before they were destroyed. This was said by al-Suddi.

His statement: ﴿And they had already promised Allah before, [that they would not turn their backs]﴾ — the verse. Concerning this there are three views:

The first: they made this covenant with Him before the Battle of the Trench (al-Khandaq) and after Badr. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: before they looked upon the confederates (al-Ahzab). This was related by al-Naqqash.

The third: before their saying, "O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you, so return."

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that they were the Banu Harithah.

﴿And the covenant of Allah will be questioned﴾ may bear two meanings:

The first: it will be questioned about, for recompense concerning it.

The second: it will be questioned for its fulfilment.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you harm or intends for you mercy?﴾ Concerning this there are three views:

The first: if He intends for you defeat (hazimah) or intends for you victory (nasr). This was related by al-Naqqash.

The second: if He intends for you punishment (adhab) or intends for you good (khayr). This was said by Qatadah.

The third: if He intends for you killing (qatl) or intends for you repentance (tawbah). This was said by al-Suddi.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verses 18–19:

Allah's words: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows those among you who hinder (others)﴾. He means the discouragers among the hypocrites. It is said they were Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions.

﴿And those who say to their brothers, "Come to us"﴾. Regarding this there are three opinions:

The first: they are the hypocrites who said to the Muslims, "Muhammad is merely a morsel for the taking, and he and those with him are doomed, so come to us."

The second: they are the Jews of Banu Qurayza, who said to their brothers among the hypocrites, "Come to us" (i.e., come to us and abandon Muhammad), for he is doomed, and if Abu Sufyan prevails he will not leave a single one of you alive.

The third: what Ibn Zayd related, that a man from among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) left his presence on the day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab) and found his brother before him with roasted meat and bread. He said, "You are like this while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is among the spears and swords!" His brother said to him, "Come to me, for you and your companion have been encircled," (the brother being from the same father and mother). He replied, "You lie, by Allah! I will certainly inform him of your affair." He went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to inform him, but found that Jibril (peace be upon him) had already descended with the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows those among you who hinder (others) and those who say to their brothers, "Come to us"﴾.

﴿And they do not come to battle except a little﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

The first: they do not attend the fighting except unwillingly, and if they do attend, their hands are with the Muslims while their hearts are with the polytheists. This is the view of Qatadah.

The second: they do not attend the fighting except for show and reputation. This is the view of al-Suddi. It is also related from al-Hasan regarding Allah's words ﴿and they do not remember Allah except a little﴾ that it was little because it was for other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Allah's words: ﴿stingy towards you﴾. Regarding this there are four interpretations:

The first: stingy with good, said by Mujahid.

The second: stingy with fighting alongside you, said by Ibn Kamil.

The third: stingy with the spoils when they obtain them, said by al-Suddi.

The fourth: stingy with spending in the way of Allah, said by Qatadah.

﴿So when fear comes﴾. Regarding this there are two statements:

The first: when fear of the enemy's fighting comes as they advance, said by al-Suddi.

The second: fear of the Prophet (ﷺ) when he prevails, said by Ibn Shajarah.

﴿You see them looking at you﴾: out of fear of fighting according to the first view, and out of fear of the Prophet (ﷺ) according to the second view.

﴿Their eyes rolling like one overcome by death﴾. This may have two meanings:

The first: their eyes roll because their minds have departed, to the point that they cannot properly look in any direction.

The second: their eyes roll from the intensity of their fear, fearing that death will come upon them from every direction.

﴿But when fear departs, they lash you with sharp tongues﴾. Regarding this there are two meanings:

(p-386) The first: they raised their voices against you with sharp tongues, that is, harsh and cutting ones. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "May Allah curse the wailing woman who raises her voice (al-saliqah), the one who tears her garment (al-khariqah), and the one who shaves her hair (al-haliqah)." By al-saliqah is meant the woman who raises her voice in lamentation, by al-khariqah the one who tears her clothing at a calamity, and by al-haliqah the one who shaves her hair.

The second: it means they harmed you with harsh speech.

Al-salq means harm, said by Ibn Qutaybah.

The poet said:

"And indeed they struck Hawazin with lances until we bowed."

Al-Khalil said: "I lashed him with the tongue when I made him hear what he disliked." Regarding their lashing you with sharp tongues there are two meanings:

The first: contending over the spoils, said by Qatadah.

The second: arguing in defence of themselves, said by al-Hasan.

﴿Stingy towards the good﴾. Regarding this there are three meanings:

The first: over the division of the spoils, said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: over the wealth they spend in the way of Allah, said by al-Suddi.

The third: over the Prophet (ﷺ) and his victory.

﴿Those have not believed﴾: meaning, in their hearts.

﴿So Allah has nullified their deeds﴾: meaning their good deeds, so that they will not be rewarded for them, because they did not seek the Face of Allah through them.

(p-387) ﴿And that was ever easy for Allah﴾. Regarding this there are two meanings:

The first: their hypocrisy was easy for Allah.

The second: the nullification of their deeds was easy for Allah.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They think the confederates have not withdrawn﴾. It means that the hypocrites think that Abu Sufyan and his confederates among the polytheists, when they dispersed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) defeated, had not gone away from him, and that they were close to them. Then there are two opinions on this:

The first: they were in that state because their fear persisted and their dismay was intense.

The second: feigning for show (riya') and continuing to be apprehensive.

﴿And if the confederates should come﴾ means Abu Sufyan and his companions among the polytheists.

﴿They would wish that they were in the desert among the Bedouins﴾ meaning the hypocrites would wish that they were out in the desert with the Bedouins, out of fear of being killed and waiting for misfortunes to befall (the Muslims).

﴿They ask about your news﴾ meaning about the news of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, saying among themselves: "Has Muhammad and his companions been destroyed? Has Abu Sufyan and his confederates prevailed?"

﴿And if they had been among you, they would not have fought except a little﴾. On this there are two opinions:

The first: except under compulsion (karhan).

The second: except for show (riya').

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 21–22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Certainly you have in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day﴾. Concerning it there are two views:

(p-388) One: that it means consolation (muwasah) at the time of fighting. This is the view of al-Suddi.

The second: an excellent example (qudwah hasanah) to be followed in it. The "excellent pattern" (al-uswah al-hasanah) is participation in the matter; it is said, "he consoles him (muwasihi) with his wealth" when he gives him a share of it.

Concerning what is meant by this, there are two views:

One: an exhortation to patience alongside the Prophet ﷺ in his battles.

The second: consolation for them in what befell them, for the Prophet ﷺ was wounded on the head, his front tooth (rubaiyyah) was broken, and his uncle Hamzah was killed.

﴿for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day﴾. Concerning it there are two views:

One: for whoever hopes for the reward of God on the Last Day. This is the view of Ibn Isa.

The second: for whoever hopes in God through his faith and believes in the Resurrection in which the deeds are recompensed. This is the view of Ibn Jubayr.

﴿And he remembers God much﴾ may bear two meanings:

One: that is, he increased in acting in obedience to Him, remembering His commands.

The second: that is, he increased in the remembrance of God, out of fear of His punishment and hope for His reward. It has been disputed who is meant by this address, on two views:

One: the hypocrites, by way of continuation from the address to them that preceded.

The second: the believers, due to His saying: ﴿for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day﴾. It has also been disputed whether this following of the Messenger is obligatory or recommended, on two views:

One: it is obligatory until there is evidence that it is recommended.

The second: it is recommended until there is evidence that it is obligatory.

It may be understood as obligatory in matters of religion and as recommended in matters of worldly affairs.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the believers saw the confederates﴾, to the end of the verse.

Concerning it there are two views:

One: that God had promised them in Surat al-Baqarah, when He said: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214], to the end of the verse.

So when they saw the confederates of the polytheists on the Day of the Trench, ﴿they said, "This is what God and His Messenger promised us"﴾. This is the view of Qatadah.

(p-389) The second: what Kathir ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr al-Muzani narrated from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "The Messenger of God ﷺ delivered a sermon in the year the confederates were mentioned, and said: 'Gabriel informed me that my community will prevail over them, meaning the palaces of al-Hirah and the cities of Kisra, so rejoice in the victory.' The Muslims rejoiced and said: 'Praise be to God, a true promise, since we were promised victory after the siege.' Then the confederates appeared, and the believers said: ﴿This is what God and His Messenger promised us﴾, to the end of the verse."

﴿in faith and submission﴾. Concerning it there are two views:

One: only faith and submission to the decree. This is the view of al-Hasan.

The second: only faith in what God promised and submission to the command of God.

The second: They are a people who had not witnessed Badr, so they covenanted with God that they would not hold back from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in any battle he witnessed or ordered, and they fulfilled what they had covenanted with God. This was said by Anas ibn Malik.

The first: Among them is one who has died, and among them is one who awaits death. This was said by Ibn Abbas, and from it is the verse of Bishr ibn Abi Khazim:

The second: Forgiving of what came before repentance, and Merciful toward what comes after it.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 26–27:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Book who supported them﴾. They were the Banu Qurayza of the Jews, who gave support (ẓāharū) to Abu Sufyan and a group of the confederates (al-aḥzāb) against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), meaning they aided him against the Messenger. The ẓihār (support, backing) is the ma'ūna (aid).

There was a covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but they broke it. So he (ﷺ) made war on them sixteen days after the Trench. Qatada said: Jibril descended upon him while he was with Zaynab bint Jahsh, washing his head, and said: "May Allah pardon you. The angels have not laid down their weapons for forty nights. March against the Banu Qurayza, for I have uprooted their tent-pegs, opened their gates, and left them in turmoil and confusion." So he marched against them and besieged them for twenty-one nights, until they came down to accept arbitration (taḥkīm) concerning themselves.

Regarding those who came down to his judgment, there are two opinions:

The first: they came down to the judgment of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and he ruled concerning them that their fighting men be killed, their dependents be taken captive, and their property (ʿaqār) go to the Muhajirun to the exclusion of the Ansar. His people said: "You have given the Muhajirun the property over us." He said: "You are the owners of property, and the Muhajirun have none." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then exclaimed "Allahu akbar" and said: "(It has been decided concerning them by the judgment of Allah)." This was related by Qatada.

The second: "They came down to the judgment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and did not make Sa'd an arbitrator. But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Sa'd and said: (Advise me concerning them.) He said: 'If you were to entrust their affair to me, I would kill their fighting men, take their dependents captive, and divide their property.' He (ﷺ) said: (By Him in whose hand my soul is, you have advised me concerning them with what Allah commanded me.)" This was narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, from his father.

﴿from their strongholds (ṣayāṣīhim)﴾: from their fortresses. The poet said:

"So the women have become stricken, and the women of Tamim have become hastening towards the ṣayāṣī."

It was so named because of their being sheltered by them. From this, the horns of cattle are called ṣayāṣī because of their protection by them, and the spur of the cock that is on its leg is called ṣīṣiyya.

﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾. Qatada said: by the doing of Jibril with them.

﴿A party you killed and a party you took captive﴾. Ata' al-Qurazi related that they were presented to the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of the Banu Qurayza, and whoever had reached puberty (iḥtalama) or whose pubic hair had grown was killed. They looked at me and my pubic hair had not grown, so I was left alone. It was said that he killed four hundred and fifty men from them, and they are those whom Allah meant by His saying ﴿a party you killed﴾, and he took captive seven hundred men, and they are those whom Allah the Exalted meant by His saying ﴿and a party you took captive﴾. Qatada said: he killed four hundred and took seven hundred captive.

﴿And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth﴾. By land he means the palm groves and cultivated fields, by homes the dwellings, and by wealth the movable property.

﴿And a land you had not trodden﴾. Concerning it there are four opinions:

The first: it is Makkah, said by Qatada.

The second: Khaybar, said by al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd.

The third: Persia and Rome, said by al-Hasan.

The fourth: whatever the Muslims would prevail over until the Day of Resurrection, said by Ikrima.

﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾. In it there are two aspects:

The first: He is competent over whatever He wills for His servants, of vengeance or pardon, said by Ibn Ishaq.

The second: He is competent over whatever He wills to open for them of fortresses and towns, said by al-Naqqash.

(p-394) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment…﴾ to the end of the verse.

This is a command from God to His Prophet that he inform his wives. The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning his giving them the choice (takhyir), in two opinions:

The first: he gave them the choice between choosing this world, in which case he would part from them, and choosing the Hereafter, in which case he would keep them. He did not give them the choice of divorce. This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

The second: he gave them the choice between divorce or remaining with him. This is the view of ʿĀ'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, ʿIkrimah, al-Sha'bi and Muqatil.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Thawr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "ʿĀ'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The verse of choice was revealed, and he began with me, the first of his wives, and said: (I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm for you in not hastening until you consult your two parents). He knew that my parents would not have commanded me to part from him. She said: Then he recited the verse of choice, and I said: Concerning this should I consult my parents? Indeed I desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode.

Then he gave the choice to all his wives, and they all said the same as I said." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Except the Himyarite woman, for she chose herself.

Scholars differed concerning the reason for which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave his wives the choice, in five opinions:

The first: because God gave His Prophet the choice between the kingdom of this world and the bliss of the Hereafter, and he chose the Hereafter over this world, and said: "O Allah, give me life as a poor man, cause me to die as a poor man, and raise me in the company of the poor (p-395)." When he chose that, God commanded him to give his wives the choice, so that they would be in the same state as him if their choice was like what he had chosen.

Abu al-Qasim al-Saymari related this.

The second: because they were jealous of him. ʿAmrah narrated from ʿĀ'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ swore that he would abandon us for a month. He entered upon me after the morning of the twenty-ninth day, and I said: O Messenger of Allah, did you not swear that you would abandon us for a month? He said: (The month is like this, and like this, and like this), then he folded down his thumb, then he said: O ʿĀ'isha, (I am going to mention a matter to you, and there is no harm for you in not hastening until you consult your two parents)." He feared for my young age. I said: And what is that? He said: (I have been commanded to give you the choice)."

The third: his wives made demands upon him, and he was unable to meet them. The first of them was Umm Salamah, who asked him for a decorated curtain, and he could not provide it. Maymunah asked him for a Yemeni garment, Zaynab bint Jahsh asked him for a striped cloak, which is the Yemeni burd, Umm Habibah asked him for a sahuli garment, Hafsah asked him for a garment of Egyptian cloth, Juwayriyah asked him for something mu'jiz, and Sawdah asked him for a Jubayri velvet. Each one of them asked for a share, except ʿĀ'isha, who asked for nothing. So God commanded that they be given the choice. This was related by al-Naqqash.

The fourth: because his wives gathered one day and said: "We want what women want of jewelry and clothing," until some of them said: "If we were with someone other than the Prophet ﷺ, then we would have status, clothing and jewelry." So God revealed the verse of choice. This was related by al-Naqqash.

The fifth: because God protected the seclusion of His Prophet, so He gave them the choice on condition that they not marry after him. When they agreed to that, he kept them.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: This was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. At that time he had nine wives besides the Himyarite woman: five from Quraysh: ʿĀ'isha, Hafsah, Umm Habibah daughter of Abu Sufyan, Umm Salamah daughter of Abu Umayyah, and Sawdah daughter of Zam'ah. These are the five from Quraysh. He also had Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab, the Himyarite, Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, and Juwayriyah bint al-Harith al-Mustaliqiyyah.

When they chose him and patience with him in what he encountered of hardship and ease, God compensated them for their patience by two matters, in return for their choice:

The first: that He made them the mothers of the believers. God said: ﴿And his wives are their mothers﴾, honoring their rights and affirming their sanctity.

The second: that He forbade him to divorce them or to exchange them. He said: ﴿Women are not lawful for you after this﴾, to the end of the verse.

So the prohibition on divorcing them was permanent.

As for the prohibition on marrying others over them, that was when the Prophet ﷺ was in hardship and had little capacity.

Then people differed, after the widening of worldly provision upon him, as to whether God made women lawful for him, in two opinions:

The first: that the prohibition on them remained in force, because God made it a reward for their patience.

The second: that God made lawful for him women, so that he could marry others over them when the world had widened upon him, because the cause of the prohibition was hardship and constraint, and when it was removed, its ruling was removed.

ʿĀ'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not die until women were made lawful for him," meaning those who had been forbidden to him. It was also said that the abrogating text for their prohibition is His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives﴾, to the end of the verse.

The first: if they choose the husband, there is no separation; if they choose themselves, it is a revocable single divorce. This is the view of al-Zuhri, ʿĀ'isha and al-Shafiʿi.

The second: if they choose the husband, it is a single divorce and he has the right of return; if they choose themselves, it is an irrevocable single divorce and the husband is like one of the suitors. This is the view of ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him.

The third: if they choose the husband, it is a single divorce and the husband is like one of the suitors; if they choose themselves, it is three divorces and she is not lawful to him thereafter until she marries another husband. This is the view of Zayd ibn Thabit. (p-397)

One: It is adultery (zina). This was said by al-Suddi.

The second: It is defiance (nushuz) and bad character. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

One: That it is the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: That they are two punishments in this world, because of the enormity of their crime in harming the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Muqatil said: Two prescribed punishments (hadd) in this world, other than theft.

Another said: If the double of a thing is its two like, then its two-fold must be four times its like.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He made their punishment double, and made the prescribed punishment (hadd) for whoever slanders them double.

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And whoever of you is obedient to Allah and His Messenger﴾, that is, obeys Allah and His Messenger; and qunut (qunut) is obedience.

Concerning it there are two opinions:

One: That both are in the Hereafter.

The second: That one of them is in this world and the other in the Hereafter.

One: In this world, because it is abundant and lawful.

The second: In the Hereafter, which is Paradise.

أحَدُهُما: يَعْنِي بِالمُسْلِمِينَ والمُسْلِماتِ المُتَذَلِّلِينَ والمُتَذَلِّلاتِ.

وَبِالمُؤْمِنِينَ والمُؤْمِناتِ المُصَدِّقِينَ والمُصَدِّقاتِ.

الثّانِي: أنَّهُما في الدِّينِ، فَعَلى هَذا في الإسْلامِ والإيمانِ قَوْلانِ:

أحَدُهُما: أنَّهُما واحِدٌ في المَعْنى وإنِ اخْتَلَفا في الأسْماءِ.

الثّانِي: أنَّهُما مُخْتَلِفانِ عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ:

أحَدُهُما: أنَّ الإسْلامَ الإقْرارُ بِاللِّسانِ، والإيمانَ التَّصْدِيقُ بِهِ، قالَهُ الكَلْبِيُّ.

(p-٤٠٣)الثّانِي: أنَّ الإسْلامَ هو اسْمُ الدِّينِ والإيمانَ هو التَّصْدِيقُ بِهِ والعَمَلُ عَلَيْهِ.

﴿والقانِتِينَ والقانِتاتِ﴾ فِيهِ وجْهانِ:

أحَدُهُما: المُطِيعِينَ والمُطِيعاتِ، قالَهُ ابْنُ جُبَيْرٍ.

الثّانِي: الدّاعِينَ والدّاعِياتِ.

﴿والصّادِقِينَ والصّادِقاتِ﴾ فِيهِ وجْهانِ:

أحَدُهُما: الصّادِقِينَ في إيمانِهِمْ والصّادِقاتِ، قالَهُ ابْنُ جُبَيْرٍ.

الثّانِي: في عُهُودِهِمْ.

﴿والصّابِرِينَ والصّابِراتِ﴾ فِيهِ وجْهانِ:

أحَدُهُما: عَلى أمْرِ اللَّهِ ونَهْيِهِ، قالَهُ ابْنُ جُبَيْرٍ.

الثّانِي: في البَأْساءِ والضَّرّاءِ.

﴿والخاشِعِينَ والخاشِعاتِ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ أوْجُهٍ:

أحَدُها: المُتَواضِعِينَ والمُتَواضِعاتِ، قالَهُ ابْنُ جُبَيْرٍ.

الثّانِي: الخائِفِينَ والخائِفاتِ: قالَهُ يَحْيى بْنُ سَلّامٍ وقَتادَةُ.

الثّالِثُ: المُصَلِّينَ والمُصَلِّياتِ، قالَهُ الكَلْبِيُّ.

﴿والمُتَصَدِّقِينَ والمُتَصَدِّقاتِ﴾ فِيهِ وجْهانِ:

أحَدُهُما: المُتَصَدِّقِينَ والمُتَصَدِّقاتِ بِأنْفُسِهِمْ في طاعَةِ اللَّهِ.

الثّانِي: بِأمْوالِهِمْ.

ثُمَّ فِيهِ وجْهانِ:

أحَدُهُما: المُؤَدِّينَ الزَّكَواتِ (zakat, the obligatory almsgiving) المَفْرُوضاتِ.

الثّانِي: المُتَطَوِّعِينَ بِأداءِ النَّوافِلِ (nawafil, voluntary acts of worship) بَعْدَ المَفْرُوضاتِ، قالَهُ ابْنُ شَجَرَةَ.

﴿والصّائِمِينَ والصّائِماتِ﴾ فِيهِ وجْهانِ:

أحَدُهُما: الإمْساكُ عَنِ المَعاصِي والقَبائِحِ.

الثّانِي: عَنِ الطَّعامِ والشَّرابِ وهو الصَّوْمُ الشَّرْعِيُّ.

وَفِيهِ وجْهانِ:

أحَدُهُما: صَوْمُ الفَرْضِ.

الثّانِي: شَهْرُ رَمَضانَ وثَلاثَةُ أيّامٍ مِن كُلِّ شَهْرٍ، قالَهُ ابْنُ جُبَيْرٍ.

وَرُوِيَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) أنَّهُ قالَ: «(صَوْمُ الشَّهْرِ وثَلاثَةُ أيّامٍ يُذْهِبْنَ وغَرَ الصَّدْرِ)».

﴿والحافِظِينَ فُرُوجَهم والحافِظاتِ﴾ فِيهِ وجْهانِ:

(p-٤٠٤)أحَدُهُما: عَنِ الفَواحِشِ.

الثّانِي: أنَّهُ أرادَ مَنافِذَ الجَسَدِ كُلَّها فَيَحْفَظُونَ أسْماعَهم عَنِ اللَّغْوِ والخَنا، وأفْواهَهم عَنْ قَوْلِ الزُّورِ وأكْلِ الحَرامِ.

وَفُرُوجَهم عَنِ الفَواحِشِ.

﴿والذّاكِرِينَ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا والذّاكِراتِ﴾ فِيهِمْ ثَلاثَةُ أوْجُهٍ:

أحَدُها: بِاللِّسانِ قالَهُ يَحْيى بْنُ سَلّامٍ.

الثّانِي: التّالُّونَ لِكِتابِهِ، قالَهُ ابْنُ شَجَرَةَ.

الثّالِثُ: المُصَلِّينَ والمُصَلِّياتِ، حَكاهُ النَّقّاشُ.

﴿أعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهم مَغْفِرَةً وأجْرًا عَظِيمًا﴾ لِعِلْمِهِمْ، قالَهُ ابْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، قالَ قَتادَةُ: وكانَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ أوَّلَ آيَةٍ نَزَلَتْ في النِّساءِ فَذُكِرْنَ بِخَيْرٍ.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decreed a matter, that they should have any choice in their affairs.﴾ Concerning it there are two opinions:

The first: "It was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh, whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed in marriage for Zayd ibn Harithah, but she refused, and her brother Abdullah ibn Jahsh also refused. They were the children of the aunt of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); their mother was Umaymah bint Abd al-Muttalib. Zayd had been a slave the day before. So this verse was revealed, and she said: 'The matter is in your hand, O Messenger of Allah,' and he married her to him." This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah.

Muqatil said: He gave her ten dinars, sixty dirhams, a wrap, a shirt, fifty mudd of food and ten mudd of dates.

The second: "It was revealed concerning Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, who was the first woman among the women to emigrate. She offered herself to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: '(I have accepted).' Then he married her to Zayd ibn Harithah, and she and her brother were displeased and said: 'We only intended the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he married us to his slave.' So this verse was revealed." This was said by Ibn Zayd.

﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾ Concerning it there are two opinions:

The first: he has certainly acted with clear injustice. This was said by Ibn Shajarah.

The second: he has certainly erred with a great error. This was said by al-Suddi and Muqatil.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 37:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when you said to him on whom Allah had bestowed favour and you had bestowed favour⟩. Qatadah, al-Suddi and Sufyan said: he is Zayd ibn Harithah, and concerning it there are two views:

One: Allah bestowed favour upon him by the love of His Messenger, and the Messenger bestowed favour upon him by adoption (tabanni).

The second: Allah bestowed favour upon him by Islam, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) bestowed favour upon him by manumission (itq).

﴿Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah⟩: meaning Zaynab bint Jahsh. This was said by al-Kalbi: "The Prophet (ﷺ) came to Zayd's house as a visitor and saw her standing, and she pleased him, so he said: (Glory be to Him who turns hearts over). When Zaynab heard that from him, she sat down." Abu Bakr ibn Ziyad said: "Zayd came to him and she told him of that, and he knew that she had fallen into his heart, so he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, permit me to divorce her, for there is pride in her, and she harms me with her tongue. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: (Fear Allah and keep your wife to yourself)." But in his heart (ﷺ) was other than that.

﴿And you concealed within yourself what Allah was to disclose⟩. Concerning it there are four sayings:

One of them: what he concealed within himself was his inclination towards her.

The second: it was an allusion to her divorce; this was said by Ibn Jurayj.

The third: he concealed within himself that if Zayd divorced her, he would marry her.

The fourth: what he concealed within himself was that Allah had informed him that she would be one of his wives before he married her; this was said by al-Hasan.

﴿And you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him⟩. Concerning it there are two views:

One: the Prophet of Allah feared the people's talk; this was said by Qatadah.

The second: he feared that he would disclose it to the people, so Allah strengthened his secret; this was said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

al-Hasan said: No verse was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) that was harder on him than this one.

Umar ibn al-Khattab said: If the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had concealed anything of the Qur'an, he would have concealed this verse, which exposed his inner matter.

﴿So when Zayd had accomplished his need of her, We gave her to you in marriage⟩. Al-watar means the attained need or desire, and here there are two sayings:

One: it is need (hajah), this was said by Muqatil.

The second: it is divorce (talaq), this was said by Qatadah.

Yahya ibn Salam said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called Zayd and said to him: (Go to Zaynab and inform her that Allah, the Exalted, has married her to me). Zayd set off and knocked at the door. She said: Who is this? He said: Zayd. She said: What need does Zayd have of me, when he has divorced me? He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has sent me to you. She said: Welcome to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and opened the door for him. He entered upon her while she was weeping, and Zayd said: May Allah not make your eye weep. You were indeed an excellent woman, if you used to fulfil my wishes, obey the command of Allah and satisfy my joy. Allah has given you in exchange something better than me. She said: Who? Woe to you! He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then she fell down in prostration to Allah, the Exalted." al-Dahhak said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her, and he was then in hardship, so he gave her as dowry a waterskin, a cloak, a hand mill and a cushion stuffed with palm fibre, and the wedding feast was dates and sawiq (roasted barley flour)."

Anas said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and entered upon her without permission." Qatadah said: "She used to boast over the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), saying: Your fathers married you off, but I was married by the Lord of the Throne, blessed and exalted."

﴿So that there will be no difficulty for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have accomplished their need of them⟩. Ibn Salam related that the polytheists said to the Prophet (ﷺ): You claim that the wife of a son is not lawful to a father, yet you have married the wife of your son Zayd. Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So that there will be no difficulty for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons⟩, meaning that Zayd was an adopted son and not a son of the loins, so the marrying of his wife was not forbidden.

﴿And the command of Allah is ever accomplished⟩: meaning the marriage of the Prophet (ﷺ) to Zaynab bint Jahsh was a binding ruling and a required decree. From this is the saying of the poet:

؎ Until, when the dust cloud of a blind trial descended, its writ was accomplished.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There is no blame upon the Prophet concerning what Allah has made obligatory for him﴾. Concerning it there are three opinions:

First: concerning what Allah made lawful for him of marrying Zaynab bint Jahsh. This was said by Muqatil.

Second: [it refers to] the woman who gave herself to the Prophet, when Allah married her to him without a dowry, but the Prophet (ﷺ) volunteered on her behalf and gave her the dowry. This was said by al-Hasan.

Third: concerning his marrying whichever women he wished, even though it is forbidden for his community to have more than four. The Jews reproached him for this, [and therefore the verse was revealed]. This was said by al-Dahhak.

(p-408) al-Tabari said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married fifteen women, consummated [marriage with] thirteen, died leaving nine, and used to divide [his time] among eight.

﴿The way of Allah with those who passed away before, and the command of Allah is a decree decreed﴾. Sunnah (sunnah, "way") means the customary practice, i.e., there is no blame upon the prophets regarding what Allah has made lawful for them, just as He made the like of this lawful for Dawud, in marrying whomever he wished, and in the woman he saw and then married, and he married a hundred women; and He made lawful for Sulayman three hundred wives and seven hundred concubines.

﴿And the command of Allah is a decree decreed﴾. In it there are two meanings:

One: a deed done; this was said by al-Dahhak.

Second: a decree decided; this is the saying of the majority.

Zaynab used to prepare the Prophet's (ﷺ) food when he intended a journey. She was the first of his wives to die during the caliphate of Umar (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhu), and she was the first woman to be carried on a bier (naʿsh), because Umar said when she died: "Alas, the Mother of the Believers is carried uncovered as men are carried!" Asma' bint Umays said: "O Commander of the Believers, I had seen in the land of Abyssinia something which provides privacy for women," and she described it to him. He ordered that it be made, and when he saw it he said: "What an excellent covering for the litter (khibaʾ al-ẓaʿīna)!"

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verses 39–40:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾. He means Zayd ibn Harithah. The polytheists said, "Muhammad has married the wife of his son," so Allah refuted them with His saying ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾, meaning he was not the father of Zayd.

(p-409) ﴿But he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets﴾. He means the last of them. ʿIsa (Jesus) will descend, and he will be a just judge and an equitable leader; he will kill the Dajjal (the Antichrist), and break the cross. Nuʿaym narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not come until there emerge liars and impostors, nearly thirty of them, each of whom claims that he is a prophet, and there is no prophet after me." Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: He did not make Muhammad the father of any of the men, because if He had made him a son, he would have made him a prophet, and there is no prophet after him. Allah said: ﴿and the Seal of the Prophets﴾.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verses 41–44:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Remember God with much remembrance﴾, concerning which there are two opinions:

One of them: Remember Him in the heart, with a constant remembrance that leads to obedience to Him and avoidance of disobeying Him.

The second: Remember God with the tongue, with much remembrance. This was said by al-Suddi.

Mujahid related from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is unable to stay awake at night to worship, is cowardly toward the enemy so that he cannot fight them, and is stingy with wealth so that he cannot spend it, then let him increase the remembrance of God, Mighty and Majestic." Concerning His mention here, there are two aspects:

One of them: supplication to Him and turning to Him in desire. This was said by Ibn Jubayr.

The second: acknowledging His lordship and confessing one's servitude to Him.

His saying: ﴿And glorify Him morning and evening﴾. Qatadah said: this refers to the Dawn prayer and the Afternoon prayer. Al-Akhfash said: al-Asil is the period between the Afternoon prayer and the night.

Al-Kalbi said: al-Asil refers to the Noon prayer, the Afternoon prayer, the Sunset prayer, and the Night prayer.

As for tasbih (glorification) here, there are three aspects:

One of them: that it is the specific tasbih, which is declaring God free from imperfection (tanzih).

The second: that it is the prayer.

The third: that it is supplication. This was said by Jarir:

"So do not neglect the glorification of the forenoon, for Yunus called upon his Lord and was rescued when he glorified Him."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [do likewise]﴾, concerning which there are four sayings:

One of them: that it is His praise. This was said by Abu al-Aliyah.

The second: His honor. This was said by Sufyan.

The third: His mercy. This was said by al-Hasan.

The fourth: His forgiveness. This was said by Ibn Jubayr.

Concerning the blessing of the angels, there are two opinions:

One of them: that it is their supplication. This was said by Abu al-Aliyah.

The second: their seeking forgiveness. This was said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

﴿That He may bring you out of darkness into light﴾. Concerning this there are three sayings:

One of them: from disbelief to faith. This was said by Muqatil.

The second: from error to guidance. This was said by Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd.

The third: from the Fire to the Garden.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verses 41–44:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Remember God with much remembrance﴾, concerning which there are two opinions:

One of them: Remember Him in the heart, with a constant remembrance that leads to obedience to Him and avoidance of disobeying Him.

The second: Remember God with the tongue, with much remembrance. This was said by al-Suddi.

Mujahid related from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is unable to stay awake at night to worship, is cowardly toward the enemy so that he cannot fight them, and is stingy with wealth so that he cannot spend it, then let him increase the remembrance of God, Mighty and Majestic." Concerning His mention here, there are two aspects:

One of them: supplication to Him and turning to Him in desire. This was said by Ibn Jubayr.

The second: acknowledging His lordship and confessing one's servitude to Him.

His saying: ﴿And glorify Him morning and evening﴾. Qatadah said: this refers to the Dawn prayer and the Afternoon prayer. Al-Akhfash said: al-Asil is the period between the Afternoon prayer and the night.

Al-Kalbi said: al-Asil refers to the Noon prayer, the Afternoon prayer, the Sunset prayer, and the Night prayer.

As for tasbih (glorification) here, there are three aspects:

One of them: that it is the specific tasbih, which is declaring God free from imperfection (tanzih).

The second: that it is the prayer.

The third: that it is supplication. This was said by Jarir:

"So do not neglect the glorification of the forenoon, for Yunus called upon his Lord and was rescued when he glorified Him."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [do likewise]﴾, concerning which there are four sayings:

One of them: that it is His praise. This was said by Abu al-Aliyah.

The second: His honor. This was said by Sufyan.

The third: His mercy. This was said by al-Hasan.

The fourth: His forgiveness. This was said by Ibn Jubayr.

Concerning the blessing of the angels, there are two opinions:

One of them: that it is their supplication. This was said by Abu al-Aliyah.

The second: their seeking forgiveness. This was said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan.

﴿That He may bring you out of darkness into light﴾. Concerning this there are three sayings:

One of them: from disbelief to faith. This was said by Muqatil.

The second: from error to guidance. This was said by Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd.

The third: from the Fire to the Garden.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 45–48:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good tidings, and a warner﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "A witness over your ummah, a bringer of good tidings of Paradise, and a warner from the Fire."

His saying: ﴿and as one who invites to Allah by His permission﴾. Concerning it there are three sayings:

The first: to the testimony that there is no god but Allah. This is what Ibn ʿAbbas said.

The second: to the obedience of Allah. This is what Ibn ʿIsa said.

The third: to Islam. This is what al-Naqqash said.

(p-411) Concerning His saying ﴿by His permission﴾ there are three aspects:

The first: by His command. This is what Ibn ʿAbbas said.

The second: by His action. This is what al-Hasan said.

The third: by the Qur'an. This is what Yahya ibn Salam said.

﴿and as a radiant lamp﴾. Concerning it there are two sayings:

The first: that it is the Qur'an, a radiant lamp, meaning illuminating, because one is guided by it. This is what Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah said.

The second: that it is the Messenger, like a radiant lamp in guidance. This is what Ibn Shajarah said, and from it is the saying of Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr:

"Indeed the Messenger is a light by which one is illuminated, a polished sword from the swords of Allah, drawn."

His saying: ﴿and give good tidings to the believers that for them is from Allah a great bounty﴾. Concerning it there are two aspects:

The first: a great reward. This is what al-Kalbi said.

The second: that it is Paradise. This is what Qatadah and al-Kalbi said. The occasion of revelation of this verse: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from al-Hudaybiyyah, Allah revealed to him ﴿Indeed We have granted you a clear victory﴾ [al-Fath: 1] and the verses after it. The Muslims said: 'Congratulations to you, O Messenger of Allah, for what Allah has given you; He has forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what followed. So what is for us, O Messenger of Allah?' Then Allah revealed: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers﴾, the verse."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾. Muqatil said: By the disbelievers he means from the people of Makkah: Abu Sufyan, ʿIkrimah, and Abu al-Aʿwar; and by the hypocrites from the people of Madinah: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, ʿAbd Allah ibn Saʿd, and Tuʿmah ibn Ubayriq. They gathered around the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, mention that our gods have intercession."

Then Allah said: ﴿and leave off their harm﴾. Concerning it there are several aspects:

The first: leave off mention of their gods, that they have intercession. This is what Muqatil said.

The second: refrain from harming them and fighting them, and this was before he was commanded to fight. This is what al-Kalbi said.

The third: its meaning is be patient over their harm. This is what Qatadah and Qutrub said.

The fourth: it is their saying "Zayd ibn Muhammad," and what they said when he married Zaynab. This is what al-Dahhak said. (p-412)
