Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 49:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾ – the verse.

The scholars are unanimous that if the divorce takes place before touching (masis) and seclusion (khalwa), there is no waiting period (iddah) for it, the divorced woman is entitled to nothing of the dower except half of it if a dower was specified for her, and there is no return (raj'ah) for the divorcer. Rather, he is like one of the suitors if his divorce is less than three.

If it is three, she is forbidden to him, and she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband.

Ata' and Jabir ibn Zayd said: if he divorces a virgin three times, it is one single divorce. This is contrary to the view of the majority.

If the divorce takes place after seclusion and before touching, there are two opinions regarding the obligation of the waiting period, the full dower, and the establishment of return:

The first, which is the view of Abu Hanifa, is that the waiting period has become obligatory, the dower has become complete, and return is established, and he treats seclusion as equivalent to touching, except that if the two are in seclusion while in the state of ihram, or fasting, or one of them is.

The second opinion, which is the position of al-Shafi'i and the one relied upon from among his statements, is that there is no waiting period, no return, and she is entitled to only half of the dower.

﴿So provide for them and release them with a fair release﴾ – the meaning of "so provide for them" is: the provision of divorce (mut'at al-talaq) in place of the dower, because a woman divorced before consummation, if she has a specified dower, has no provision; and if she has no specified dower, then in place of half of the specified amount she has a provision (mut'ah) that stands in place of the specified amount, which varies according to the wealth and poverty of the husband. Hammad estimated it as half the equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl). Abu 'Abd Allah al-Zaydi said: the highest of it is a servant, its middle is a garment, and its lowest is whatever has a price.

As for the one who has been consummated with, there are two opinions regarding her entitlement to the provision from the dower:

The first: she has no provision in addition to receiving the full dower.

The second: she is entitled to the provision upon divorce, and she is entitled to the dower by the marriage.

Regarding His saying ﴿and release them with a fair release﴾ there are two aspects:

The first: that it is the giving of the provision according to the ease and hardship (of the husband), as said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: that it is divorcing her while she is in a state of purity without having had intercourse, as said by Qatada.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 50:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives whose bridal payments (ujur) you have given﴾, meaning their dowries (sadaq). On this there are three opinions:

First: Lawful to him by this verse are his first wives who were with him before the revelation of this verse. This is the view of Mujahid.

As for making other women lawful, that is not the case, because of His saying: ﴿Women are not lawful to you after this﴾.

Second: By this verse He made all women lawful to him, and by it He abrogated (naskh) His saying ﴿Women are not lawful to you after this﴾.

Third: By it He made lawful those women whom He named in it, and not those whom He did not name in His saying.

﴿And what your right hand possesses﴾, meaning the slave women.

﴿From what Allah has bestowed on you as spoils﴾, meaning from the spoils of war. Among the slave women was Mariyah, the mother of his son Ibrahim.

From what Allah bestowed on him was Safiyyah and Juwayriyah. He freed them and married them.

﴿And the daughters of your paternal uncles, the daughters of your paternal aunts, the daughters of your maternal uncles, and the daughters of your maternal aunts﴾. This was said by Ubayy ibn Ka'b. Then He said: ﴿who emigrated with you﴾. On this there are two opinions:

(p-414) One: It means Muslim women.

Two: It means women who emigrated (muhajirat) to Madinah.

Abu Salih narrated from Umm Hani, who said: "This verse was revealed, and the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to marry me, but he was forbidden from me because I had not emigrated." Scholars differed about emigration (hijrah) on two views:

One: It is a condition for the lawfulness of women for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whether they are from distant or near kin, so that he may not marry anyone except an emigrant woman.

Two: It is a condition for the lawfulness of the daughters of his paternal uncles and aunts mentioned in the verse, and it is not a condition for the lawfulness of unrelated women.

﴿And a believing woman, if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾. The people of interpretation differed over whether there was a woman with the Prophet (ﷺ) who gave herself to him, on two views:

One: No woman gave herself to him. This is the view of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. The interpretation of the one who reads إنْ وُهِبَتْ (in wuhibat, with a kasrah on the hamzah and a dammah on the wa and the ta, in the passive) is to be understood as referring to the future.

Two: There was a woman with him who gave herself to him. This is the view of the majority. The interpretation of the one who reads إنْ وَهَبَتْ with a fatḥah (in wahabat, active) is that it refers to a specific woman: whenever she gives herself, it becomes lawful for him to marry her. The one who reads إنْ وَهَبَتْ with a kasrah (in wa hibat, meaning the verb is read with the particle as a conditional) understands it as referring to every woman who gives herself, that it is lawful for him to marry her.

There was disagreement about the woman who gave herself to him, on four opinions:

One: She was Umm Sharik bint Jabir ibn Dabab, and she was a righteous woman. This was said by Urwah ibn al-Zubayr.

Two: She was Khawlah bint Hakim. This is the view of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her.

Three: She was Maymunah bint al-Harith. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

(p-415) Four: She was Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, Umm al-Masakin, a woman of the Ansar.

This was said by al-Sha'bi.

﴿If the Prophet wishes to marry her, it is exclusively for you, not for the believers﴾. On this there are three opinions:

One: It is exclusively for him that, if she gives herself to him, he may marry her without the consent of a guardian (wali) and without a dowry.

This is not so for anyone among the believers. This was said by Qatadah.

Two: It is exclusively for him that, if she gives herself to him, he is not obliged to pay her a dowry. This is not so for anyone else among the believers. This was said by Anas ibn Malik and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib.

Three: It is exclusively for him to possess the contract of marriage by the wording of a gift (hibah). This is not so for anyone else among the believers. This was said by al-Shafi'i.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿We have indeed known what We have prescribed for them concerning their wives﴾. On this there are three interpretations:

One: We prescribed that no woman may marry except with a guardian and two witnesses.

Two: We prescribed that a man may not exceed four wives. This is the view of Mujahid.

Three: We prescribed for them, on behalf of the women, maintenance (nafaqah) for them and the equitable division (qasm) among them.

This was said by some of the jurists.

﴿Or what their right hands possess﴾, meaning that these may be lawful to him without a limited number and without an obligatory division. ﴿So that there will be no discomfort upon you﴾. On this there are two opinions:

One: It refers back to His saying: ﴿Indeed We have made lawful to you your wives﴾. This was said by Ibn Isa.

Two: It refers to His saying: ﴿And a believing woman, if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾. This seems to be the view of Yahya ibn Sallam.

Allah's statement, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them, and take to yourself whom you will﴾. Regarding it there are four interpretations:

First: You divorce whichever of your wives you will and keep whichever of them you will. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

Second: You leave off marrying whomever you will and marry whomever you will. This was said by al-Hasan.

Third: You withdraw from whichever of your wives you will and do not go to her, and you go to whichever of your wives you will and do not withdraw from her. This was said by Mujahid.

This interpretation indicates that the qasm (the equal allocation of nights among the wives) was waived for him.

Fourth: You delay whichever of your wives you will, and take to yourself whichever of them you will. This was said by Qatadah.

Mansur narrated from Ibn Razin, who said: "Some of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ heard that he intended to release them, so they came to him and said: 'Do not release us, and you are free to do as you wish concerning us, between us and you.' So he postponed some of them and took others to himself. Among those he postponed were Juwayriyah, Maymunah, Umm Habibah, Safiyyah and Sawdah. And he would allot to them from himself and from his property as he wished. Among those he took to himself were Aisha, Hafsah, Umm Salamah and Zaynab, and his allotment of his property and of himself among them was equal."

﴿And whomever you seek out from those you had set aside﴾: that is, whomever you seek, taking him to yourself, from those you had set aside, that you should bring him to yourself.

﴿there is no blame upon you﴾: concerning this there are two views:

One: there is no blame upon you regarding whom you sought out, nor regarding whom you set aside. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Second: there is no blame upon you in taking to yourself whom you had set aside. This was said by Mujahid.

﴿That is more suitable that their eyes may be comforted and they will not grieve and will be pleased with what you have given them, all of them﴾: concerning it there are four aspects:

First: when they know that he will not divorce them, their eyes are comforted and they do not grieve.

Second: when they know that he will not marry others over them, their eyes are comforted and they do not grieve. This was said by Qatadah.

Third: when they know that this is from the command of Allah the Exalted concerning them, their eyes are comforted and they do not grieve. This was said by Qatadah.

Fourth: that they knew he had the right to return them to his bed if he withdrew from them, so their eyes are comforted and they do not grieve. This was said by Mujahid.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 52:

His words, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take women after this﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions:

The first: It is not lawful for you to take women after your wives whom you gave the choice, and they chose God and His Messenger and the Last Abode (p-417).

Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah said: They are the nine, and it was restricted to them and prohibited from others than them.

The second: It is not lawful for you to take women after that which We made lawful for you by Our saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives whom you have given their bridal payments﴾, to His saying: ﴿and a woman who gives herself to the Prophet﴾, the verse.

The permission after his wives was restricted to the daughters of his paternal uncle, the daughters of his paternal aunts, the daughters of his maternal uncle, and the daughters of his maternal aunts who emigrated with him. This was said by Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.

The third: It is not lawful for you to take women from among non-Muslim women, such as Jewish women, Christian women and polytheist women, while whatever others there are of Muslim women is lawful. This was said by Mujahid.

﴿Nor is it allowed that you exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions:

The first: And not that you exchange Muslim women for polytheist women. This was said by Mujahid.

The second: Do not divorce your wives in order to substitute for them whoever's beauty pleases you. This was said by al-Dahhak.

It was said that the one whose beauty pleased him was Asma bint ʿUmays, after the killing of Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib, concerning her.

The third: And not that you exchange your wives for the wives of others, for the Arabs in the Jahiliyyah would swap their wives: one of them would give his wife to a man and take in exchange his wife in place of her. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

(p-418) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you﴾. The occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of this verse is what Abu Nadra narrated from Anas ibn Malik: "The Prophet ﷺ passed by some of his wives, and with them were men conversing. He disliked that, and when he disliked something it was recognised in his face. When evening came, he went out, ascended the pulpit, and recited this verse."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿for a meal, without waiting for its preparation﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

First: not waiting for it to be cooked. This was said by al-Dahhak and Mujahid.

Second: not anticipating its time and hour. This was said by Qatada.

﴿Nor remaining for conversation﴾. Abu Qilaba narrated from Anas:

He said: When Zaynab bint Jahsh was brought as a gift (in marriage) to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he prepared food and invited a people. They entered while Zaynab was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they began conversing, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept going out and returning while they were still sitting. So Allah, Exalted, revealed: ﴿And when you have eaten, then disperse﴾.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is an offence to the Prophet, and he feels shy of you﴾, meaning the Prophet ﷺ feels shy about informing you (to leave).

﴿But Allah is not shy of the truth﴾, that He should command you with it.

﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

First: a need, said by al-Suddi.

Second: the pages of the Qur'an, said by al-Dahhak.

Third: a loan (ariya), said by Muqatil.

Their meanings are close.

(p-419) ﴿Ask them from behind a screen﴾. The wives of the Prophet and all other women were commanded to veil from the sight of men, and men were commanded to lower their gaze from women.

Regarding the cause of the veil there are three sayings:

The first is what Mujahid narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "I was eating with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from a bowl of hays (a mixture of dates, butter and cheese). Umar passed by and he called him, and he ate, and his finger touched my finger. Umar said: 'If you were obeyed regarding them, no eye would see them.' Then the verses of the veil were revealed."

The second is what Urwa ibn al-Zubayr narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "The wives of the Prophet ﷺ used to go out at night to the open places (al-mabaddi), a wide open area where they relieved themselves. Umar would say to the Prophet ﷺ: 'Veil your wives, O Messenger of Allah!' But he did not do so. Then Sawda bint Zam'a went out one night, and she was a tall woman, and he called out to her in a loud voice: 'We have recognised you, O Sawda!' out of eagerness that the veil be revealed." She said: "So Allah, Exalted, revealed the veil."

Then the verse was revealed: ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾.

﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾. This may bear two meanings:

First: purer for them from doubt (rayba).

Second: purer for them from desire (shahwa).

﴿It is not for you to offend the Messenger of Allah, nor to marry his wives after him, ever﴾. Second: it is obligatory, because it is an act of worship, even if no permission follows it.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 55:

His words, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers or their sons﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions:

One of them: There is no blame upon them in abandoning the veil (ḥijāb).

This is the view of Qatadah.

The second: It concerns removing the outer garment (jilbāb), as said by Mujahid.

﴿Nor their brothers, nor the sons of their brothers, nor the sons of their sisters﴾. Al-Sha'bi said: He did not mention the paternal uncle because he may be lawful to his son, so he would describe her to him.

﴿Nor their women﴾. Regarding this there are two aspects:

One of them: It means Muslim women, not polytheist women, as said by Mujahid.

The second: That it applies to all women.

﴿Nor what their right hands possess﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions:

One of them: It refers to female slaves only, not male slaves, as said by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib.

The second: That it is general, covering both female and male slaves.

Those who hold this view differed concerning what is permitted to the male slave, on two opinions:

One of them: What is permitted to the relatives within the forbidden degrees, such as fathers and sons, is what lies beyond the navel and below the knee, because she is forbidden to him just as she is forbidden to them.

The second: That which the coat of mail does not cover of the exposed part of her body, as said by Ibrahim.

This is because the slave, although forbidden to her at present, may become lawful to her through manumission at a later time.

The occasion of the revelation of this verse is what al-Kalbi related: when the verse of the veil was revealed, ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾, the fathers and sons stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we also do not speak to them except from behind a screen." So this verse was revealed.

The Almighty's statement: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾. Concerning it there are three opinions:

The first: Allah's blessing upon him is His praise of him in the presence of the angels, and the angels' blessing is supplication. This was said by Abu al-'Aliyah.

The second: Allah's blessing upon him is His forgiveness of him, and the angels' blessing is their seeking forgiveness for him. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The third: Allah's blessing upon him is His mercy, and the angels' blessing is their supplication for him. This was said by al-Hasan, and it is the meaning of the statement of 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah.

The fourth: their blessing upon him is that they bless him? This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace⁠﴾. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla narrated, saying: Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah met me and said: "Shall I give you a gift that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" I said: "Yes."

He said: "We asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, we already know how to greet you with peace, so how is the blessing upon you?' He said: (Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Abraham and upon the family of Abraham; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.

O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham; indeed You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.)"  (p-422) Abu al-'Abbas Tha'lab said: The meaning of our saying "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad" is: increase Muhammad in blessing and mercy. The interpretations mentioned above apply to it.

As for His statement, the Exalted: ﴿and greet him with peace, a greeting﴾, it may have two meanings:

One of them: submit to His command with obedience to Him, in full submission.

The second: greet him with peace through supplication for him, a greeting of peace, that is, saying "Peace."

Muqatil related, saying: When this verse was revealed, the Muslims said: "Then what is for us, O Messenger of Allah?" So there was revealed: ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels⁠﴾, and the verse.

The commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-‘Uyun) on surah 33, verses 57–58:

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, those who annoy Allah and His Messenger—Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter﴾. Regarding them there are three opinions:

The first: they are the makers of images (al-tasawir). This was said by ‘Ikrimah.

The second: they are those who slandered the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he took Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab (as a wife). This was said by Ibn ‘Abbas.

The third: they are a group of the hypocrites who used to lie against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and accuse him falsely. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Regarding His words ﴿who annoy Allah and His Messenger﴾ there are three aspects:

The first: its meaning is "who annoy the friends of Allah."

The second: He made the harming of His Messenger (ﷺ) a harming of Himself, to honour his station.

The third: it is what has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: The son of Adam insults Me, though it is not fitting for him to insult Me, and he denies Me, though it is not fitting for him to deny Me. As for his insulting Me, it is his saying, 'Allah has a son.' And as for his denying Me, it is his saying, 'I will not resurrect anyone after death.'"

The curse of this world is killing and expulsion, and the curse of the Hereafter is the Fire.

His exalted words: ﴿And those who annoy believing men and believing women﴾, the verse.

Regarding whom this verse was revealed there are three opinions:

The first: it was revealed concerning the fornicators, who used to walk about, see a woman, and make gestures at her. This was said by al-Kalbi.

The second: it was revealed concerning a people who used to harm ‘Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and lie about him. This was said by Muqatil and al-Naqqash.

The third: it was revealed concerning those who spoke of ‘A’ishah and Safwan ibn al-Mu‘attal with the slander (al-ifk). This was said by al-Dahhak.

Qatadah related that ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, recited it one night, and it frightened him so much that he set out to Ubayy and said: "O Abu al-Mundhir, I recited the Book of Allah and it struck me in every place."

﴿And those who annoy believing men and believing women without their having earned it﴾. By Allah, I punish them and beat them. He said: "You are not one of them. You are only a disciplinarian (mu'addib), you are only a teacher (mu'allim)."

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 59–62:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They should draw their outer garments close around themselves﴾, concerning which there are three opinions:

One: that al-jilbab is the rida' (outer wrap), said by Ibn Mas'ud and al-Hasan.

The second: that it is the qina' (veil), said by Ibn Jubayr.

(p-424) The third: that it is every garment a woman wears over her clothes, said by Qutrub.

Concerning drawing their jalabib close over themselves, there are two opinions:

One of them: that she binds it above her head and lets it fall over her khimar until the opening of her chest is not seen, said by Ikrimah.

The second: that she covers her face so that only her left eye is visible, said by Ubaydah al-Salmani.

﴿That is more suitable that they will be known and not be harmed﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

One: that they may be known as free women, distinct from slave women.

The second: that they may be known as chaste, distinct from women who display themselves.

Qatadah said: When a slave woman passed by, the hypocrites would harass her, so God forbade free women to imitate slave women.

His saying: ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist, and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾. Concerning them there are two opinions:

One: that they are the fornicators, said by Ikrimah and al-Suddi.

The second: that they are the people of immorality and vileness, said by Salamah ibn Kuhayl.

Concerning His saying ﴿If the hypocrites do not desist﴾ there are two opinions:

One: from harassing the women of the Muslims, said by al-Kalbi.

The second: from manifesting what is in their hearts of hypocrisy, said by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

﴿And those who spread rumours in the city﴾. Concerning them there are three opinions:

One: that they are those who pursue women in large numbers and approach them, said by al-Suddi.

The second: that they are those who relate reports by which the hearts of the believers are weakened and the hearts of the polytheists are strengthened, said by Qatadah.

The third: that al-irjaf is the seeking of strife, said by Ibn Abbas; the rumours were so named because of the agitation of voices concerning them and the people's rushing into them.

﴿Then We will surely incite you against them﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations:

One: its meaning is "We will surely empower you over them," said by Ibn Abbas.

(p-425) The second: "We will surely inform you about them," said by al-Suddi.

The third: "We will surely move you to take them to task," which is the meaning of Qatadah's saying.

﴿Then they will not remain as your neighbours therein except briefly﴾. It was said: this means their expulsion from it; and it was said: what is excepted is the interval between his saying to them "Get out!" and their departure.

His saying: ﴿The way of Allah concerning those who passed away before, and you will not find in the way of Allah any change﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions:

One: meaning His way concerning them is that whoever manifests polytheism is killed, said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: His way concerning them is that whoever commits fornication is punished with the hadd, which is the meaning of al-Suddi's saying.

The third: His way concerning them is that whoever manifests hypocrisy is banished, said by Qatadah.

﴿And you will not find in the way of Allah any change﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations:

One: meaning transformation and alteration, related by al-Naqqash.

The second: meaning that one who is killed justly has no blood-money owed for him upon his killer, said by al-Suddi.

Third: the nobles (al-ashraf), as said by Tawus.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verse 69:

His words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who abused Moses﴾. Its meaning: do not harm Muhammad, lest you become like those who harmed Moses.

Concerning what they harmed His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ with, there are two opinions:

One of them: their saying "Zayd ibn Muhammad" (Zayd being the son of Muhammad), related by al-Naqqash.

The second: "The Prophet ﷺ made a distribution, and a man from the Ansar said: 'This distribution was not intended for the sake of Allah.' This was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he became angry and said: 'May Allah have mercy on Moses; he was harmed with more than this and he was patient.'" This was related by Abu Wa'il.

Concerning what Moses (peace be upon him) was harmed with, there are three opinions:

(p-427) The first: they accused him of sorcery and madness.

The second: what Abu Hurayrah related from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Moses was a man who was shy and very modest; not a bit of his skin could be seen, out of his shyness. Those among the Children of Israel who harmed him said: 'He only conceals himself because of a defect in his skin or body, either leprosy, or a swelling of the testicles, or some other affliction.' Allah wished to clear him of what they said. One day Moses was alone, and he placed his garments on a rock and bathed. When he finished, he came to take his garment, but the rock ran off with his clothes. Moses pursued it until he came to a group of the Children of Israel, and they saw him naked, most beautiful of men in form. Thus Allah cleared him of what they said."

The third: what Ibn Abbas related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that Moses and Aaron ascended the mountain, and Aaron died. The Children of Israel said: "You killed him; he was gentler to us than you and more beloved." So they harmed him with this. Allah commanded the angels, and they carried him and passed by an assembly of the Children of Israel, and the angels spoke of his death. Then they buried him, and no one knew the location of his grave except the vulture. Allah made him deaf and mute. Aaron died before Moses in the wilderness, and Moses died two months before the end of the period of wandering.

﴿And he was honored in the sight of Allah﴾. Concerning this there are three aspects:

One: that he was the accepted one; this was said by Ibn Zayd.

The second: because his supplication was answered; this was said by al-Hasan.

The third: because he never asked Allah for anything except that He gave it to him, up to the point of the vision; this was said by Ibn Sinan.

Qutrub said: "Wajih" is derived from "wajh" (face), because it is the most elevated part of the body.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verses 70–71:

His saying: ﴿And speak words of appropriate justice﴾. Concerning it there are six interpretations:

First: "justice" ('adl), said by al-Suddi.

Second: "truth" (sidq), said by Qatadah.

(p-428) Third: "correctness" (sawab), said by Ibn Isa.

Fourth: it is the saying "There is no god but Allah" (la ilaha illa Allah), said by Ikrimah.

Fifth: it is that whose outward form agrees with its inward reality.

Sixth: that it is what is intended thereby the face of Allah alone, and nothing else.

It may also bear a seventh meaning: that it is reconciliation between those who are quarrelling, and it is derived from aligning an arrow (tasdid al-sahm) so that the target may be struck by it.

﴿He will set right for you your deeds﴾. Concerning it there are two interpretations:

One of them: He will set them right by accepting them.

The second: by granting success (tawfiq).

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 33, verses 72–73:

His words: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains﴾ On it there are five opinions:

The first: this trust is what Allah, glory be to Him, commanded regarding obedience to Him and forbade regarding disobedience to Him. This was said by Abu al-'Aliyah.

The second: it is the laws and rulings that Allah made obligatory upon the servants, and this is close to the first. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Ibn Jubayr.

The third: it is the entrusting of men and women with their private parts (furuj). This was said by Ubayy.

It is also said that the first thing Allah created from Adam was the private part, and He said: ("O Adam, this is a trust I have deposited with you, so do not wear it except in its right. If you guard it, I will guard you.")

The fourth: it is the trusts that people entrust to one another, and the first of them was Adam's entrusting his son Qabil with his family and offspring when he wished to set out to obey his Lord; Qabil then betrayed the trust by killing his brother Habil. This was said by al-Suddi.

The fifth: this trust is the evidences of His lordship that Allah deposited in the heavens, the earth, the mountains, and the creation, that they should manifest them. They manifested them, except for humankind, which concealed and denied them. This was said by some of the theologians (mutakallimun).

Regarding the offering of this trust there are three opinions:

The first: its offering means the command to what must be done to preserve it, and the great sin in neglecting it. This was said by some of the theologians.

The second: the trust was presented in opposition to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, so it was heavier than them, due to the severity of its rulings, and they could not bear it and were too weak to carry it. This was said by Ibn Bahr.

The third: Allah offered its burden so that entry into it would be after knowledge of it.

Those who say this differ on two points:

One: it was offered to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid.

(p-430) The second: it was offered to the inhabitants of the heavens, the inhabitants of the earth, and the inhabitants of the mountains among the angels. This was said by al-Hasan.

﴿So they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it﴾ may have two meanings:

One: they refused to bear it out of inability, and were apprehensive of it out of fear.

The second: they refused to bear it out of caution, and were apprehensive of it out of fear of falling short.

﴿And man bore it﴾ On this there are two views:

One: all of humankind. This was said by Tha'lab.

The second: it was Adam, and then it passed from him to his offspring. This was said by al-Hasan.

It is narrated from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan, that when the trust was offered to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, they said: "And what is in it?" It was said to them: "If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do evil, you will be punished." They said: "No."

Mujahid said: When Allah created Adam, He offered it to him, and he said: "And what is it?" He was told: ("If you do well, I will reward you, and if you do evil, I will punish you.") He said: "I have taken it up, O Lord."

Mujahid said: The time between his taking it up and his leaving the Garden was no more than the interval between the midday prayer and the afternoon prayer.

﴿Indeed, he was ever wrongdoing, ignorant﴾ On this there are three aspects:

One: wrongdoing toward himself, ignorant of his Lord. This was said by al-Hasan.

The second: wrongdoing in his sin, ignorant regarding what he laid upon his offspring after him. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The third: wrongdoing toward its right. This was said by Qatadah.

Ignorant of the outcome of his affair. This was said by Ibn Jurayj.

His words: ﴿That Allah may punish the hypocrite men and hypocrite women and the polytheist men and polytheist women﴾ On this there are two opinions:

One: that He punishes them for polytheism and hypocrisy. This is the meaning of the statement of Muqatil.

The second: for their betrayal of the trust. al-Hasan said: They are the two who wronged it, and the two who betrayed it: the hypocrite and the polytheist.

﴿And that Allah may accept the repentance of the believing men and believing women﴾ meaning He overlooks them for discharging the trust and fulfilling the covenant.

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ toward whoever repents from his polytheism, ﴿Merciful﴾ by guiding them to His obedience. And Allah knows best.
